title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
大哉堯之爲君也巍巍乎唯天爲大唯堯
則之蕩蕩乎民無能名焉
楊謨
同考試官教諭陳　批　〔揭書出題偶得論語是章塲中士子率多講堯獨能如此而於他聖人少貶殊戾本旨此〕
〔作灼有定見且詞氣舂容宜錄以範後學〕
考試官教諭粘　批　〔摹寫堯德配天民難形容意出〕
考試官教諭劉　批　〔文字順整〕
===
聖人贊前聖君德之大必言其所以爲大也盖
至大而不可以言語形容者天也前聖之德同
之夫豈人之所能名哉想昔夫子之意以爲人
君居天下之大位貴有首天下之大德載觀堯
之爲君也以首出庶物之資膺皇天眷命之重
誠至大而無以復加焉何以言之哉彼天下之
物莫高於山也而天無不覆莫大於地也而天
無不容盖巍巍乎其高且大矣惟堯也欽明文
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

大哉，堯之爲君也！巍巍乎！唯天爲大，唯堯則之。蕩蕩乎！民無能名焉。

楊謨

同考試官教諭陳批：〔揭書出題，偶得論語是章。塲中士子率多講堯獨能如此，而於他聖人少貶，殊戾本旨。此〕〔作灼有定見，且詞氣舂容，宜錄以範後學。〕

考試官教諭粘批：〔摹寫堯德配天、民難形容意出。〕

考試官教諭劉批：〔文字順整。〕

聖人贊前聖君德之大，必言其所以爲大也。盖至大而不可以言語形容者，天也；前聖之德同之，夫豈人之所能名哉！想昔夫子之意，以爲人君居天下之大位，貴有首天下之大德。載觀堯之爲君也，以首出庶物之資，膺皇天眷命之重，誠至大而無以復加焉。何以言之哉？彼天下之物，莫高於山也，而天無不覆；莫大於地也，而天無不容。盖巍巍乎其高且大矣！惟堯也，欽明文
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“Great indeed was Yao as a ruler! How lofty! Heaven alone is great, and Yao alone took it as his model. How boundless! The people could find no words to describe him.”

Yang Mo

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: 〔On opening the book to select a topic, we happened upon this chapter of the Analects. Most candidates in the examination argued that Yao alone could attain this, thereby somewhat disparaging the other sages—a marked departure from the passage’s original meaning. This〕〔composition clearly shows a firm grasp of the matter; its diction and tone are also measured and ample. It should be recorded as a model for later students.〕

Comment by Examiner Nian, Instructor: 〔It brings out the meaning that Yao’s virtue matched Heaven and was difficult for the people to describe.〕

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: 〔The writing is fluent and orderly.〕

When the Sage praises the greatness of an earlier sage ruler’s virtue, he must explain what made it great. For that which is supremely great and cannot be described in words is Heaven. The virtue of the earlier sage was like it: how could people find words to describe it? I imagine that the Master’s meaning in those days was that a ruler, occupying the highest position in the world, ought above all to possess the great virtue that stands foremost in the world. Now consider Yao as a ruler. With qualities that set him above all beings, he received the weighty charge bestowed by August Heaven’s favor. He was indeed supremely great, beyond anything that could be added to him. How can this be explained? Among the things of this world, nothing is higher than the mountains, yet there is nothing Heaven does not cover; nothing is greater than the earth, yet there is nothing Heaven does not contain. How lofty indeed are its height and greatness! Yao alone, reverent, enlightened, and cultured…

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
思之德足以代乎天而理物較而言之同一其
尊無對也何有於差殊乎允恭克讓之懿足以
奉乎天而弘化合而觀之均一其大無外也殆
與之齊等乎夫至大惟天堯之德既有以配之
矣故其積之盛也有以光被乎四表其流之長
也有以昭格乎上下蓋蕩蕩乎其廣且遠矣當
時被耕田鑿井之休者但付帝力於何有而已
欲言德而不能盡其廣猶言天而不能盡其高
也孰得而形容之哉沐遷善敏德之化者但罔
===
帝則於不知而已將語德而不能盡其遠猶語
天而不能盡其大也孰得而名狀之哉是則天
本至大也德同乎天而自難乎其爲大民非不
欲名也德恊於民而自不知其所以爲名所謂
大哉者如此夫嘗觀堯之大固不可名然成功
文章亦可見其緒也書言欽明文思而首以欽
發義授舜以中之一言則其德或有可知然亦
不過敬以行其常道而已而正唯其不可及也
敬其體而中其用乎大其極矣夫子祖述於堯
punctuated: 思之德，足以代乎天而理物，較而言之，同一其尊無對也，何有於差殊乎？允恭克讓之懿，足以奉乎天而弘化，合而觀之，均一其大無外也，殆與之齊等乎！夫至大惟天，堯之德既有以配之矣，故其積之盛也，有以光被乎四表；其流之長也，有以昭格乎上下。蓋蕩蕩乎其廣且遠矣！當時被耕田鑿井之休者，但付帝力於何有而已。欲言德而不能盡其廣，猶言天而不能盡其高也，孰得而形容之哉？沐遷善敏德之化者，但罔帝則於不知而已。將語德而不能盡其遠，猶語天而不能盡其大也，孰得而名狀之哉？是則天本至大也，德同乎天，而自難乎其爲大；民非不欲名也，德恊於民，而自不知其所以爲名。所謂大哉者如此夫！嘗觀堯之大，固不可名，然成功文章，亦可見其緒也。《書》言「欽明文思」，而首以欽發義；授舜以中之一言，則其德或有可知。然亦不過敬以行其常道而已，而正唯其不可及也。敬其體而中其用乎？大其極矣！夫子祖述於堯
translation_en: …and thoughtfulness: these virtues suffice for him to act on Heaven’s behalf and bring order to all things. Comparing them, both are equally exalted and without peer; what difference could there be? His admirable sincerity, reverence, and capacity for yielding suffice for him to serve Heaven and extend its transforming influence. Considered together, both are equally great and without limit. Surely he stands Heaven’s equal! Heaven alone is supremely great, and Yao’s virtue was already sufficient to match it. Thus, in the fullness of its accumulation, its radiance reached the four quarters; in the enduring course of its influence, it shone upon and reached all above and below. Vast indeed were its breadth and reach! Those who then enjoyed the blessings of tilling their fields and digging their wells simply said, “What has the emperor’s power to do with us?” To speak of his virtue without being able to encompass its breadth is like speaking of Heaven without being able to encompass its height. Who could give it adequate expression? Those who received his transforming influence, turning toward goodness and striving diligently in virtue, simply followed the emperor’s standards without knowing it. To speak of his virtue without being able to encompass its reach is like speaking of Heaven without being able to encompass its greatness. Who could describe or name it? Heaven, then, is inherently supremely great. His virtue was the same as Heaven, and its greatness was consequently difficult to express [?]. It was not that the people did not wish to name it: his virtue accorded with the people, yet they themselves did not know how to name it. Such is the meaning of “Great indeed!” I have considered that although Yao’s greatness assuredly cannot be named, its traces can nevertheless be seen in his accomplished works and splendid cultural forms. The Book of Documents speaks of his “reverence, intelligence, refinement, and thoughtfulness,” placing reverence first to bring out the meaning. He passed on to Shun the single word “centrality”; thus something of his virtue may be known. Yet this amounted to no more than reverently practicing the constant Way—and precisely therein lay what others could not attain. Was reverence its substance and centrality its application? His greatness reached the utmost! The Master took Yao as his ancestral model…

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
而事功過之論者亦擬於天而稱爲時中之聖
則是敬爲聖學始終之要而中爲百聖傳心之
法希聖者當合而觀之
詩云鳶飛戾天魚躍于淵言其上下察也
王命
同考試官訓導路　批〔說理文字最難下筆一騁浮詞便不相似此篇詞理俱到作中庸義當如是矣〕
同考試官學正程　批〔此作本或問立說且詞語典實其深於理學者歟〕
===
考試官教諭粘　批〔見理精深用詞明當錄之〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔文有發明〕
中庸引詩而釋之所以明道無不在之實也蓋
無物不體道之用廣也而其所以然者則至隱
存焉中庸發明費隱之意於是至矣昔子思子
論君子之道始於夫婦之能知能行極於聖人
天地之所不能盡可謂至矣而猶未盡也故引
旱麓之詩曰莫高匪天而鳶之飛戾焉莫浚匪
淵而魚之躍出焉詩人言此豈泛焉而無所指
punctuated:
而事功過之。論者亦擬於天，而稱爲時中之聖。則是敬爲聖學始終之要，而中爲百聖傳心之法，希聖者當合而觀之。

詩云：「鳶飛戾天，魚躍于淵。」言其上下察也。
王命
同考試官訓導路批〔說理文字最難下筆，一騁浮詞，便不相似。此篇詞理俱到，作中庸義當如是矣。〕
同考試官學正程批〔此作本或問立說，且詞語典實，其深於理學者歟？〕
考試官教諭粘批〔見理精深，用詞明，當錄之。〕
考試官教諭劉批〔文有發明。〕

中庸引詩而釋之，所以明道無不在之實也。蓋無物不體，道之用廣也；而其所以然者，則至隱存焉。中庸發明費隱之意，於是至矣。昔子思子論君子之道，始於夫婦之能知能行，極於聖人天地之所不能盡，可謂至矣，而猶未盡也。故引旱麓之詩曰：「莫高匪天，而鳶之飛戾焉；莫浚匪淵，而魚之躍出焉。」詩人言此，豈泛焉而無所指
translation_en:
…yet his achievements surpassed those of Yao. Commentators likewise compared him to Heaven and called him the sage who attained centrality as circumstances required. Thus reverence is essential to the learning of sages from beginning to end, while centrality is the method by which all sages transmit their understanding of the mind. Those who aspire to sagehood should consider the two together.

The Book of Odes says: “The kite flies up to Heaven; the fish leaps in the depths.” This speaks of its manifest presence above and below.
Wang Ming 王命

Associate Examiner Lu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “Writing that expounds principle is the hardest to undertake. Once one indulges in empty phrases, it ceases to resemble what it should be. This essay succeeds in both expression and principle. An exposition of the Doctrine of the Mean ought to be like this.”
Associate Examiner Cheng, Instructor, comments: “This essay bases its argument on Questions and Answers [on the Doctrine of the Mean], and its language is classical and substantial. Is its author perhaps deeply versed in the learning of principle?”
Examiner Nian, Instructor, comments: “Its understanding of principle is precise and profound, and its wording clear. It should be selected.”
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “The essay offers illuminating insights.”

The Doctrine of the Mean quotes the Book of Odes and explains it in order to make clear the reality that the Way is present everywhere. For there is nothing it does not embody: the functioning of the Way is far-reaching. Yet that which makes things so lies in the utmost hiddenness. Here the Doctrine of the Mean brings its elucidation of the Way’s extensiveness and hiddenness to its fullest expression. When Master Zisi discussed the Way of the noble man, he began with what ordinary husbands and wives can know and practice, and extended it to what even sages and Heaven and Earth cannot exhaust. This could be called the furthest reach, yet even then the subject was not exhausted. Thus he quoted the ode “At the Foot of Mount Han”: “Nothing is higher than Heaven, yet the kite flies up to it; nothing is deeper than the depths, yet the fish leaps out of them.” In saying this, could the poet have spoken vaguely, with nothing particular in view…

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
哉誠以盈天地之間無往而非物總天下之物
無一而非道彼鳶乃凡物之一也鳶之飛必戾
于天者豈徒飛哉化育之著於上者于鳶之飛
而見之也魚亦凡物之一也魚之躍必出于淵
者豈徒躍哉氣機之動於下者于魚之躍而見
之也自夫鳶而觀之則凡具聲色貌象而散殊
於宇宙之間者何者而非斯道之所在自夫魚
而觀之則凡爲屈伸聚散而充斥於坱圠之内
者何者而非斯道之所存徹上徹下洋洋乎流
===
動而充滿吾道之全體蓋於是而無遁形矣于
彼于此優優乎充塞而無間吾道之妙用蓋至
是而無餘藴矣凡此者皆道之費也而其所以
然者則隱而莫之見焉道不可離之意不於是
而益明乎抑論之道者率性之謂無物不有無
時不然固衆人之所能知能行者也子思子特
指鳶魚言之者蓋亦姑借二物以形容其無所
不在之實耳然非學者此心之存不至於馳鶩
高遠而他求則亦目爲麁迹而不知求矣此子
punctuated: 哉？誠以盈天地之間，無往而非物；總天下之物，無一而非道。彼鳶乃凡物之一也，鳶之飛必戾于天者，豈徒飛哉？化育之著於上者，于鳶之飛而見之也。魚亦凡物之一也，魚之躍必出于淵者，豈徒躍哉？氣機之動於下者，于魚之躍而見之也。自夫鳶而觀之，則凡具聲色貌象而散殊於宇宙之間者，何者而非斯道之所在？自夫魚而觀之，則凡爲屈伸聚散而充斥於坱圠之内者，何者而非斯道之所存？徹上徹下，洋洋乎流動而充滿，吾道之全體蓋於是而無遁形矣。于彼于此，優優乎充塞而無間，吾道之妙用蓋至是而無餘藴矣。凡此者，皆道之費也，而其所以然者，則隱而莫之見焉。道不可離之意，不於是而益明乎？抑論之，道者，率性之謂，無物不有，無時不然，固衆人之所能知能行者也。子思子特指鳶魚言之者，蓋亦姑借二物以形容其無所不在之實耳。然非學者此心之存，不至於馳鶩高遠而他求，則亦目爲麁迹而不知求矣。此子
translation_en:
…could it be so? Indeed, throughout the space between Heaven and Earth, there is nowhere without things; and among all the things under Heaven, there is not one without the Way. The kite is but one among the myriad things. When it flies and necessarily reaches the heavens, is this merely flight? The work of transformation and nurture manifest above becomes visible in the kite’s flight. The fish, too, is one among the myriad things. When it leaps and necessarily emerges from the depths, is this merely leaping? The activity of the vital force below becomes visible in the fish’s leap. Viewed through the kite, among all things possessing sound, color, appearance, and form, dispersed in their diversity throughout the universe, which is not a place where this Way resides? Viewed through the fish, among all things that contract and expand, gather and disperse, filling the vast expanse, which does not contain this Way? Penetrating above and below, flowing abundantly and filling all, the Way we follow is here revealed in its entire substance, with nothing concealed. Here and there, amply filling everything without a gap, its wondrous operation now leaves no potential unexpressed. All these are the Way’s extensive manifestations; yet that which makes them so remains hidden and unseen. Does this not make still clearer the meaning of the assertion that the Way cannot be departed from?
To consider the matter further: the Way means following one’s nature. No thing is without it, and at no time is it otherwise. It is indeed something ordinary people can know and practice. Master Zisi singles out the kite and fish merely to borrow these two things to describe the reality of the Way’s presence everywhere. Yet unless learners preserve this mind, they will either race after what is lofty and distant, seeking elsewhere, or regard these things as mere coarse traces and fail to know that they should seek the Way in them. This Master …

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
程子所以有有事正心之説而朱子喫緊爲人
之論深致意也不然則下文誠明之功推而至
於聖人天道之極致無以復加矣何以繼之曰
下學立心之始
君仁莫不仁君義莫不義君正莫不正一
正君而國定矣
張湘
同考試官學正蔣　批〔題本親切作者於仁義正字只主心上泛説殊非孟子本意〕〔間有知者又辭不達〕
考試官教諭粘　批〔儒先謂此篇主言人臣當以正〕〔君爲急此作得之〕
晚得此卷議論精當噫格心之學端有望於子矣
考試官教諭劉　批〔莫不仁義正字內俏入行〕〔政貫講良是〕
大賢論事君格心之爲大而正君之爲要也夫
君心出治之本格心所以正君也知格心之效
爲大則知正君之爲要矣孟子言此其示人臣
以知要也歟蓋嘗論之君心之非害治之本也
punctuated:
程子所以有「有事正心」之説，而朱子「喫緊爲人」之論深致意也。不然，則下文誠明之功，推而至於聖人天道之極致，無以復加矣，何以繼之曰「下學立心之始」？

君仁，莫不仁；君義，莫不義；君正，莫不正。一正君而國定矣。
張湘

同考試官學正蔣　批〔題本親切，作者於仁義正字，只主心上泛説，殊非孟子本意。〕〔間有知者，又辭不達。〕
考試官教諭粘　批〔儒先謂此篇主言人臣當以正〕〔君爲急，此作得之。〕晚得此卷，議論精當。噫！格心之學，端有望於子矣！
考試官教諭劉　批〔莫不仁義正字內俏入行〕〔政貫講，良是。〕

大賢論事君，格心之爲大，而正君之爲要也。夫君心，出治之本；格心，所以正君也。知格心之效爲大，則知正君之爲要矣。孟子言此，其示人臣以知要也歟？蓋嘗論之：君心之非，害治之本也。
translation_en:
…This is why Master Cheng spoke of “having as one’s task the rectification of the mind,” and why Master Zhu’s discussion of “earnestly working for others’ benefit” dwelt so deeply upon it. Otherwise, the work of sincerity and illumination discussed below, extended to the utmost attainment of the sage and the Way of Heaven, would admit of nothing further. Why, then, follow it with the words “the beginning of learning from things below and establishing the mind”?

“If the ruler is benevolent, none will fail to be benevolent; if the ruler is righteous, none will fail to be righteous; if the ruler is correct, none will fail to be correct. Once the ruler is rectified, the state will be settled.”
Zhang Xiang

Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, School Director: 〔The topic itself bears directly on practical concerns. In treating the words ‘benevolent,’ ‘righteous,’ and ‘correct,’ the author confines himself to generalities about the mind. This is quite contrary to Mencius’s original intent.〕〔Where he occasionally shows understanding, his wording fails to convey it.〕

Comment by Examiner Nian, Instructor: 〔Earlier Confucian scholars said that this passage chiefly teaches that a minister should make rectifying〕〔the ruler his urgent concern. This composition grasps that point.〕 I obtained this script late; its argument is incisive and apt. Ah! In the learning devoted to rectifying the ruler’s mind, there is indeed reason to place hope in you!

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: 〔Within the words ‘none will fail to be benevolent, righteous, and correct,’ he deftly introduces the conduct of〕〔government [?], carrying it through the exposition. This is very sound.〕

The great worthy discusses serving the ruler: rectifying his mind is the great task, and setting the ruler right is the essential concern. The ruler’s mind is the source from which government proceeds; rectifying his mind is the means of setting the ruler right. To recognize the greatness of the effects of rectifying his mind is to recognize the essential importance of setting the ruler right. In saying this, was Mencius teaching ministers to discern what is essential? Let us consider the matter: errors in the ruler’s mind are the root of harm to government.

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
大人格心善治之要也是故仁為君心之固有
而欲常蔽焉格之則仁存矣君仁則德愛宣布
而用人行政之皆仁豈有違其心而不仁者乎
義亦君心之固有而私每勝焉格之則義立矣
君義則斷制不爽而用人行政之皆當豈有反
所好而不義者乎仁義既純於心則有天理之
正無人欲之邪而君正於上矣仁義既達於外
則正朝廷以正百官正百官以正萬民而罔不
一於正矣大人格心之效如此其大是以人臣
===
不必瑣瑣於紛更也惟在啓心格心以凊萬化
之源不必屑屑於强諫也惟在正已正君以端
庶政之本夫非心未格則理欲相勝而國之治
亂未可知也一正君而大本立無事人之與適
也必進君子必退小人有日新月盛之幾君明
臣良而治自無不成矣格心未至則始終難保
而國之安危未可必也君一正而萬事從不煩
政之與間也善政必行弊政必革無朝更夕改
之患綱舉目張而國自無不定矣是則欲治國
punctuated: 大人格心，善治之要也。是故仁為君心之固有，而欲常蔽焉，格之則仁存矣。君仁則德愛宣布，而用人行政之皆仁，豈有違其心而不仁者乎？義亦君心之固有，而私每勝焉，格之則義立矣。君義則斷制不爽，而用人行政之皆當，豈有反所好而不義者乎？仁義既純於心，則有天理之正，無人欲之邪，而君正於上矣。仁義既達於外，則正朝廷以正百官，正百官以正萬民，而罔不一於正矣。大人格心之效如此其大，是以人臣不必瑣瑣於紛更也，惟在啓心格心，以凊萬化之源；不必屑屑於强諫也，惟在正已正君，以端庶政之本。夫非心未格，則理欲相勝，而國之治亂未可知也。一正君而大本立，無事人之與適也，必進君子，必退小人，有日新月盛之幾，君明臣良，而治自無不成矣。格心未至，則始終難保，而國之安危未可必也。君一正而萬事從，不煩政之與間也，善政必行，弊政必革，無朝更夕改之患，綱舉目張，而國自無不定矣。是則欲治國
translation_en:
For a great man to rectify the ruler’s heart is the essential means of achieving good government. Benevolence is inherent in the ruler’s heart, yet desires constantly obscure it; once the heart is rectified, benevolence is preserved. When the ruler is benevolent, his virtue and loving concern spread abroad, and his employment of men and conduct of government are alike benevolent. How could anyone act contrary to his heart and fail to be benevolent? Righteousness, too, is inherent in the ruler’s heart, yet selfishness frequently overcomes it; once the heart is rectified, righteousness is established. When the ruler is righteous, his decisions are unerring, and his employment of men and conduct of government are alike fitting. How could anyone oppose what he favors and fail to be righteous? Once benevolence and righteousness are pure within his heart, there is the correctness of heavenly principle and none of the perversity of human desires: the ruler above is thereby upright. Once benevolence and righteousness extend outward, he rectifies the court so as to rectify the hundred officials, and rectifies the hundred officials so as to rectify the myriad people, until all are united in uprightness.

So great is the effect of a great man’s rectification of the ruler’s heart. Thus a minister need not busy himself with a welter of changes; his task lies solely in opening and rectifying the ruler’s heart, thereby clearing [?] the source of all transforming influences. Nor need he expend himself on forceful remonstrance; his task lies solely in rectifying himself [?] and rectifying the ruler, thereby setting right the foundation of all governmental affairs. If the errors of the ruler’s heart remain unrectified, principle and desire contend for mastery, and whether the state will be well governed or disordered cannot yet be known. Once the ruler is rectified, however, the great foundation is established, and there is no need to find fault with individual men [?]. Gentlemen will assuredly be advanced and petty men dismissed. There will be the promise of daily renewal and monthly flourishing; with an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers, good government will naturally be achieved.

If rectification of the heart remains incomplete, constancy from beginning to end is difficult to ensure, and the state’s security or peril cannot be determined with certainty. Once the ruler is upright, however, all affairs follow accordingly, and there is no need to criticize individual measures [?]. Beneficial policies will assuredly be implemented and defective ones reformed, without the trouble of changing things in the morning and revising them again in the evening. When the main cord of the net is lifted, its meshes spread open: the state will naturally become settled. Thus, those who wish to govern the state…

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
者先正其君欲正君者先格其心爲大臣者可
不知其要乎然非有大人之德則亦莫之能正
也雖然格君固大人事也然以孔孟而不能行
於齊魯之君何哉盖君無受善之地雖大人亦
莫如之何也已矣故臣道在脩德而積誠君道
當虛心以求益然後上下交而德業成矣孟子
言此雖爲大臣發也而君人者亦宜有警也夫
易
忠信所以進德也
張湘
===
同考試官學正蔣　批〔題似易而難作忠信二字是進德之目所以進德處又不宜多講知本旨者或窘於詞〕
〔騁浮詞者或昧於理此篇體認親切敷演詳明無一蔓言蕪語讀之令人起敬噫子其潛心易學而有得者歟〕
考試官教諭粘　批〔忠信二字融會本義成文〕
可嘉
考試官教諭劉　批〔講所進德處無工夫最是〕
君子實其心之所主所以益其心之所得也盖
punctuated:
者先正其君，欲正君者先格其心。爲大臣者，可不知其要乎？然非有大人之德，則亦莫之能正也。雖然，格君固大人事也，然以孔孟而不能行於齊魯之君，何哉？盖君無受善之地，雖大人亦莫如之何也已矣。故臣道在脩德而積誠，君道當虛心以求益，然後上下交而德業成矣。孟子言此，雖爲大臣發也，而君人者亦宜有警也夫！

易
忠信所以進德也。
張湘

同考試官學正蔣，批〔題似易而難作，忠信二字是進德之目，所以進德處又不宜多講。知本旨者或窘於詞，〕〔騁浮詞者或昧於理。此篇體認親切，敷演詳明，無一蔓言蕪語，讀之令人起敬。噫！子其潛心易學而有得者歟！〕
考試官教諭粘，批〔忠信二字融會本義成文。〕可嘉。
考試官教諭劉，批〔講所進德處無工夫，最是。〕

君子實其心之所主，所以益其心之所得也。盖
translation_en:
…must first rectify their ruler; those who wish to rectify their ruler must first correct his heart. Can those serving as great ministers fail to understand this essential point? Yet without the virtue of a great man, none can rectify him. Even so, correcting the ruler is indeed the business of a great man; why, then, could even Confucius and Mencius not put this into practice with the rulers of Qi and Lu? It was because those rulers had no disposition to accept goodness: even a great man could do nothing about them. Thus the minister’s way lies in cultivating virtue and accumulating sincerity, while the ruler’s way requires an open mind in seeking improvement. Only then can those above and below communicate, and virtue and achievement be brought to fulfillment. Although Mencius spoke these words for great ministers, those who rule over others should also take warning from them!

Book of Changes
“Loyalty and trustworthiness are the means of advancing virtue.”
Zhang Xiang

Associate Examiner Jiang, School Director, comments: 〔The topic seems easy but is difficult to write on. ‘Loyalty’ and ‘trustworthiness’ name the particular means of advancing virtue; yet how they advance virtue should not be discussed at excessive length. Those who understand the fundamental purport may find themselves at a loss for words,〕〔while those who indulge in ornate language may fail to grasp the principle. This essay shows an intimate understanding and develops its argument fully and clearly, without a single rambling phrase or superfluous expression. Reading it inspires respect. Ah! You must be one who has devoted himself to studying the Changes and gained insight from it!〕
Examiner Nian, School Instructor, comments: 〔The essay integrates the fundamental meaning of ‘loyalty’ and ‘trustworthiness’ into its composition.〕Praiseworthy.
Examiner Liu, School Instructor, comments: 〔It is entirely right that the discussion of the virtue being advanced does not introduce a separate program of cultivation.〕

The gentleman makes sincere that upon which his heart is centered; this is how he increases what his heart has attained. For…

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
理之得于心者德也心有不實則無地以居之
德何由而進乎此君子之進德必以忠信爲主
也歟昔文言申乾九三乾乾惕厲之意以爲君
子之心固勤於進德而進德之本寔在於忠信
蓋忠者盡己而已心有不盡則妄念乘之而起
矣故君子之心一主於盡己而他無所適凡志
意之所向念慮之所發者一皆出自衷悃而無
少僞妄罄厥丹扃而無一隱伏求其自歉也去
其自欺也是非忠乎信者以實而已心有不實
===
則眞念因之而鑿矣故君子之心惟以實爲主
而無時不在凡物之感于外情之應于中者一
皆斷斷誠一而虛假不作慥慥篤實而眞念常
存表裏如一也始終不渝也是非信邪君子之
忠信如此豈非所以進德哉蓋天下之理得於
忠而失於僞惟忠也則理有所依而立故凡志
之所向將駸駸上達可大之勢自不能禦天理
日明也人欲日消也忠非所以進德乎天下之
道立于信而廢于欺惟信也則道有所據而安
punctuated: 理之得于心者，德也。心有不實，則無地以居之，德何由而進乎？此君子之進德必以忠信爲主也歟！昔《文言》申乾九三乾乾惕厲之意，以爲君子之心固勤於進德，而進德之本寔在於忠信。蓋忠者，盡己而已。心有不盡，則妄念乘之而起矣。故君子之心一主於盡己，而他無所適。凡志意之所向、念慮之所發者，一皆出自衷悃而無少僞妄，罄厥丹扃而無一隱伏。求其自歉也，去其自欺也，是非忠乎？信者，以實而已。心有不實，則眞念因之而鑿矣。故君子之心惟以實爲主，而無時不在。凡物之感于外、情之應于中者，一皆斷斷誠一而虛假不作，慥慥篤實而眞念常存。表裏如一也，始終不渝也，是非信邪？君子之忠信如此，豈非所以進德哉？蓋天下之理得於忠而失於僞。惟忠也，則理有所依而立。故凡志之所向，將駸駸上達，可大之勢自不能禦。天理日明也，人欲日消也，忠非所以進德乎？天下之道立于信而廢于欺。惟信也，則道有所據而安。
translation_en:
…Principle apprehended in the heart is virtue. If the heart lacks sincerity, principle has no place to dwell: how, then, can virtue advance? Is this not why the gentleman must make wholeheartedness and trustworthiness the foundation of his advancement in virtue? In elucidating the meaning of unremitting diligence and vigilant caution in the third yang line of the Qian hexagram, the Commentary on the Words of the Text (Wenyan) held that the gentleman’s heart is indeed diligent in advancing virtue, but that the foundation of such advancement truly lies in wholeheartedness and trustworthiness.

Wholeheartedness means simply giving fully of oneself. If the heart holds anything back, wayward thoughts seize the opportunity to arise. Thus the gentleman’s heart is devoted entirely to giving fully of himself and turns nowhere else. Whatever his intentions aim toward and whatever thoughts he forms all spring from his innermost sincerity, without the slightest falsity or delusion. He opens his sincere heart completely, leaving nothing concealed. He seeks out what leaves him dissatisfied with himself [?] and eliminates his self-deception. Is this not wholeheartedness?

Trustworthiness means simply being true. If the heart lacks truthfulness, its genuine thoughts are thereby damaged. Thus the gentleman’s heart takes truthfulness alone as its guiding principle and never departs from it. Whenever things affect him from without and feelings respond within, all is resolutely sincere and undivided, with no falsehood arising; all is earnestly substantial and true, with genuine thoughts ever present. Inner and outer are alike; from beginning to end he does not waver. Is this not trustworthiness? With the gentleman’s wholeheartedness and trustworthiness being such, are they not the means of advancing virtue?

The principles of all under Heaven are apprehended through wholeheartedness and lost through falsity. Only with wholeheartedness does principle have something on which to rest and become established. Thus, wherever his intentions turn, he will advance steadily toward higher understanding, and the impetus toward greatness will of itself be irresistible. Heavenly principle grows clearer each day, and human desires diminish each day. Is wholeheartedness not the means of advancing virtue? The Way of all under Heaven is established through trustworthiness and undone through deception. Only with trustworthiness does the Way have something on which to rest securely…

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
故凡力之所致皆鑿鑿有得日新之益自不容
已高明可極也廣大可致也信非所以進德乎
夫忠信乃實心也德乃實理也以實心而求實
理宜無不進矣苟無實心則理與心拂將扞格
而難入雖終日乾乾何益於得邪此忠信所以
為進德之本而為君子之所務也歟竊嘗論之
天下之理皆具於易而聖人之立言一取于易
觀乾坤二卦之文言殆可見矣盖乾之體健而
實坤之體順而虛健而實則有主誠就業之心
===
順而虛則有固執持守之意故聖人於乾之九
三則曰忠信以進德立誠以居業於坤之六二
則曰敬以直內義以方外是盖取健順二體之
義豈鑿空杜撰之言邪先正以易為萬世文字
之祖詎不信夫
天地之道貞觀者也日月之道貞明者也
天下之動貞夫一者也
韓建偉
同考試官學正蔣　批　此題發明吉凶貞勝之義士
punctuated:
故凡力之所致，皆鑿鑿有得，日新之益自不容已。高明可極也，廣大可致也，信非所以進德乎？夫忠信乃實心也，德乃實理也，以實心而求實理，宜無不進矣。苟無實心，則理與心拂，將扞格而難入，雖終日乾乾，何益於得邪？此忠信所以為進德之本，而為君子之所務也歟！竊嘗論之：天下之理皆具於易，而聖人之立言一取于易，觀乾坤二卦之文言，殆可見矣。盖乾之體健而實，坤之體順而虛，健而實則有主誠就業之心，順而虛則有固執持守之意。故聖人於乾之九三則曰：「忠信以進德，立誠以居業。」於坤之六二則曰：「敬以直內，義以方外。」是盖取健順二體之義，豈鑿空杜撰之言邪？先正以易為萬世文字之祖，詎不信夫！

天地之道，貞觀者也；日月之道，貞明者也；天下之動，貞夫一者也。

韓建偉

同考試官學正蔣　批：此題發明吉凶貞勝之義，士
translation_en:
…Thus, wherever one directs one’s efforts, one makes definite gains, and the benefits of daily renewal cannot cease. Loftiness and illumination can be attained to their utmost; breadth and greatness can be achieved. Is trustworthiness not therefore a means of advancing virtue? Wholeheartedness and trustworthiness constitute a genuine heart, while virtue constitutes real principle. Seeking real principle with a genuine heart, one should invariably advance. Without a genuine heart, principle and the heart conflict; obstruction makes it difficult for principle to enter. Though one strives diligently all day, what benefit would this bring toward attainment? This is why wholeheartedness and trustworthiness are the foundation for advancing virtue and what the gentleman devotes himself to!

I have ventured to consider this: all the principles of the world are contained in the Book of Changes, and the sages drew their teachings entirely from it. This may readily be seen in the Commentary on the Words of the Text for the hexagrams Qian and Kun. Qian is vigorous and substantial in its constitution; Kun is compliant and receptive. Vigor and substantiality give rise to the resolve to make sincerity one’s guiding principle and accomplish one’s work; compliance and receptivity give rise to the intention to hold firmly and maintain what one has embraced. Thus, concerning the nine in the third place of Qian, the sage says: “Through wholeheartedness and trustworthiness, advance virtue; by establishing sincerity, abide in one’s work.” Concerning the six in the second place of Kun, he says: “Through reverence, straighten what is within; through righteousness, square what is without.” These sayings draw upon the meaning of the two constitutions, vigor and compliance. How could they be baseless fabrications? A worthy predecessor called the Book of Changes the ancestor of all writing for ten thousand generations. Is this not indeed true?

“The way of Heaven and Earth is constant in its manifestation; the way of the sun and moon is constant in its illumination; the movements of all under Heaven are constant in the One.”

Han Jianwei 韓建偉

Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang 蔣, Instructor: “This topic elucidates the meaning of ‘good and ill fortune prevail through constancy.’ Scholars …”

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
予亦能言之但於貞字處多不知旨獨此作發揮明白
讀其文可以知其藴矣
考試官教諭粘　批〔講天人之理明瑩可取〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔潔淨精微可與言易矣〕
大傳論造化人事之理皆正而有常所以明易
之理也夫造化人事即易理之攸寓也合而觀
之則易之理居然可見矣昔吾夫子傳易論吉
凶之貞勝而推言其理謂夫理妙於卦爻雖隱
而難知理見於天人則顯而可驗何則天位乎
===
上地位乎下天地之變化雖不能無通復也而
其爲道則一貞觀而已仰觀乎天垂象於高明
者確然有常而機緘之畢露俯察乎地效法於
博厚者隤然有定而槖籥之自彰萬古此天地
萬古此貞觀無變更也豈幽深玄遠而不可測
耶日臨乎晝月臨乎夜日月之運行雖不能無
盈縮也而其爲道則一貞明而已瞻彼日兮懸
象於中天者本體常存赫然其莫掩瞻彼月兮
照耀乎下土者清光可掬烱然其自如萬古此
punctuated:
予亦能言之，但於貞字處多不知旨，獨此作發揮明白，讀其文可以知其藴矣。
考試官教諭粘批〔講天人之理，明瑩可取。〕
考試官教諭劉批〔潔淨精微，可與言易矣。〕
大傳論造化人事之理，皆正而有常，所以明易之理也。夫造化人事，即易理之攸寓也。合而觀之，則易之理居然可見矣。昔吾夫子傳易，論吉凶之貞勝，而推言其理，謂夫理妙於卦爻，雖隱而難知；理見於天人，則顯而可驗。何則？天位乎上，地位乎下。天地之變化，雖不能無通復也，而其爲道，則一貞觀而已。仰觀乎天，垂象於高明者，確然有常，而機緘之畢露；俯察乎地，效法於博厚者，隤然有定，而槖籥之自彰。萬古此天地，萬古此貞觀，無變更也，豈幽深玄遠而不可測耶？日臨乎晝，月臨乎夜。日月之運行，雖不能無盈縮也，而其爲道，則一貞明而已。瞻彼日兮，懸象於中天者，本體常存，赫然其莫掩；瞻彼月兮，照耀乎下土者，清光可掬，烱然其自如。萬古此
translation_en:
…I too can speak of it [?], but in treating the word zhen—correctness and constancy—most fail to grasp its purport. This composition alone expounds it clearly; reading it, one can understand its deeper meaning.
Examiner Nian, Instructor, comments: 〔Its discussion of the principles of Heaven and humanity is lucid and worthy of approval.〕
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔Pure, precise, and subtle: its author is someone with whom one may discuss the Book of Changes.〕
The Great Commentary discusses the principles governing the transformations of nature and human affairs: all are correct and constant. In this way it elucidates the principles of the Book of Changes. For the transformations of nature and human affairs are precisely where the principles of the Changes reside. Viewed together, they make those principles readily apparent. Formerly, when our Master composed his commentary on the Changes, he discussed how good and ill fortune prevail through constancy, and extended his explanation of the underlying principle. His meaning was that, although principle is subtle within the hexagrams and their lines, hidden and difficult to comprehend, when manifested in Heaven and humanity it is evident and open to verification. Why is this so?
Heaven occupies the place above, and Earth the place below. Although their transformations necessarily involve passage and return [?], their Way consists solely in constant, correct manifestation. Looking upward at Heaven, whose images hang in its lofty brightness, we find it firm and constant, its workings fully revealed. Looking downward at Earth, which displays its patterns in its breadth and depth, we find it yielding and settled, its generative workings—like those of a bellows—manifest of themselves. Through all ages, Heaven and Earth remain thus; through all ages, their constant, correct manifestation undergoes no alteration. How could this be something obscure, profound, mysterious, and remote, beyond our power to fathom?
The sun presides over the day, and the moon over the night. Although their movements necessarily involve increase and decrease, their Way consists solely in constant, correct brightness. Behold the sun, its image suspended in mid-heaven: its essential substance endures, its radiance impossible to obscure. Behold the moon, shining upon the earth below: its pure light seems something one could gather in one's hands, its brilliance freely shining forth. Through all ages, these…

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
日月萬古此貞明無滅息也豈窈冥昏黙而不
可見耶造化如此而况於人事乎故天下之動
或見於物之相感也一物有一物之情萬物有
萬物之情物不一而情之所遷亦不一也或見
於事之相錯也一事有一事之變萬事有萬事
之變事無窮而變之所之亦無窮也然物情雖
不一也而物之理有至一者存順之則吉逆之
則凶歷千萬世而其揆皆同是順逆者情之異
趨理之正而有常宜順不宜逆者則惟一端也
===
與天地之道夫何異乎事變雖無窮也而事之
理有不變者在從之則吉違之則凶通千萬人
而其應不爽是從違者變之殊途理之正而莫
易可從不可違者則固一致也與日月之道又
何疾乎吁造化人事正常之理如此此卦爻吉
凶所以貞勝而不已者盖亦理之常也大傳翼
易之旨不其至哉抑論有造化之易有人事之
易有易書之易天地日月之道造化之易也天
下之動人事之易也吉凶之貞勝易書之易也
punctuated: 日月，萬古此貞明，無滅息也，豈窈冥昏黙而不可見耶？造化如此，而况於人事乎？故天下之動，或見於物之相感也。一物有一物之情，萬物有萬物之情，物不一，而情之所遷亦不一也。或見於事之相錯也。一事有一事之變，萬事有萬事之變，事無窮，而變之所之亦無窮也。然物情雖不一也，而物之理有至一者存，順之則吉，逆之則凶，歷千萬世而其揆皆同。是順逆者，情之異趨；理之正而有常，宜順不宜逆者，則惟一端也。與天地之道夫何異乎？事變雖無窮也，而事之理有不變者在，從之則吉，違之則凶，通千萬人而其應不爽。是從違者，變之殊途；理之正而莫易，可從不可違者，則固一致也。與日月之道又何疾乎？吁！造化人事正常之理如此，此卦爻吉凶所以貞勝而不已者，盖亦理之常也。大傳翼易之旨，不其至哉？抑論有造化之易，有人事之易，有易書之易。天地日月之道，造化之易也；天下之動，人事之易也；吉凶之貞勝，易書之易也。
translation_en:
…sun and moon; through all ages, this steadfast brightness never ceases. How could it be obscure, dark, and imperceptible? If this is so in the workings of creation, how much more so in human affairs? Thus, the movements of all under Heaven may appear in the mutual responsiveness of things. Each thing has its own disposition, and the myriad things have their myriad dispositions. Things differ, and so too do the directions in which their dispositions shift. These movements may also appear in the interweaving of affairs. Each affair has its own changes, and the myriad affairs have their myriad changes. Affairs are inexhaustible, and so too are the directions their changes take. Yet although the dispositions of things differ, there is an ultimate unity in their underlying principle. Following it brings good fortune; opposing it brings misfortune. Through countless generations, the standard remains the same. Following and opposing are divergent tendencies of dispositions; but the correctness and constancy of principle—that one should follow it and not oppose it—are one alone. How does this differ from the Way of Heaven and Earth?

Although changes in affairs are inexhaustible, there is something unchanging in their underlying principle. Complying with it brings good fortune; departing from it brings misfortune. Among countless people, its responses never fail. Compliance and departure are different paths taken amid change; but the correctness and immutability of principle—that it may be followed but must not be transgressed—are fundamentally one. How, again, does this differ [?] from the Way of the sun and moon? Ah! Such is the correct and constant principle of creation and human affairs. That good and ill fortune in the hexagrams and their lines continually prevail through constancy is likewise, surely, an expression of the constancy of principle. Is not the Great Commentary’s purpose in elucidating the Book of Changes supremely profound?

To discuss this further, there are the changes of creation, the changes of human affairs, and the changes presented in the Book of Changes. The Way of Heaven and Earth, sun and moon, constitutes the changes of creation; the movements of all under Heaven constitute the changes of human affairs; and the prevailing of good and ill fortune through constancy constitutes the changes presented in the Book of Changes.

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
易之爲書原於造化達於人事合天人而一之
者也學者明於造化之理而察於人事之故觀
夫卦爻之變而玩夫吉凶之占則於易之理其
庶幾乎
書
同寅協恭和衷哉
楊謨
同考試官教諭陳　批〔皐陶安民之謨其事似涉於粗迹然寅恭皆是自心上作工夫其理至爲精密作者不知率易視之有失〕
===
考試官教諭粘　批〔講和衷處意思甚好〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔文字典則〕
君臣一心而民則以正大臣陳安民之謨也夫
民則未易正也非君臣敬畏之同其能有所爲
哉皐陶陳安民之謨於舜如此謂夫典禮雖出
於天而惇庸則在於我使其君臣之間承天意
以從事而寅畏有未同則情睽而道不行矣相
上帝以綏猷而恭敬有未協則怠勝而事不立
punctuated:
易之爲書，原於造化，達於人事，合天人而一之者也。學者明於造化之理，而察於人事之故，觀夫卦爻之變，而玩夫吉凶之占，則於易之理，其庶幾乎！
書
同寅協恭和衷哉。
楊謨
同考試官教諭陳　批〔皐陶安民之謨，其事似涉於粗迹，然寅恭皆是自心上作工夫，其理至爲精密。作者不知，率易視之，有失。〕
考試官教諭粘　批〔講和衷處，意思甚好。〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔文字典則。〕
君臣一心，而民則以正。大臣陳安民之謨也。夫民則未易正也，非君臣敬畏之同，其能有所爲哉？皐陶陳安民之謨於舜如此，謂夫典禮雖出於天，而惇庸則在於我。使其君臣之間，承天意以從事，而寅畏有未同，則情睽而道不行矣；相上帝以綏猷，而恭敬有未協，則怠勝而事不立。
translation_en:
The Changes, as a book, originates in the workings of creation and extends to human affairs, uniting Heaven and humanity as one. If students understand the principles of creation, discern the circumstances of human affairs, observe the changes of the hexagrams and their lines, and ponder the prognostications of good and ill fortune, will they not come close to understanding the principles of the Changes?
Book of Documents
“Be united in reverence, concerted in respect, and harmonious at heart!”
Yang Mo
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “Gao Yao’s counsel for bringing peace to the people appears to concern relatively superficial outward actions. Yet reverence and respect both involve working upon the heart, and their principles are exceedingly subtle and precise. The author fails to recognize this and treats the matter casually: this is a fault.”
Examiner Nian, Instructor, comments: “The thought expressed in the discussion of harmony at heart is very good.”
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “The writing is classical and conforms to established standards.”
When ruler and ministers are of one heart, the standards of conduct among the people are thereby rectified. This is a great minister setting forth his counsel for bringing peace to the people. Now, the people’s standards of conduct are not easily rectified. Unless ruler and ministers share the same reverence and awe, how can they accomplish anything? Such was the counsel Gao Yao presented to Shun for bringing peace to the people. His meaning was that, although the established institutions and rites issue from Heaven, making them substantial and putting them into practice rest with us. If ruler and ministers undertake their work in obedience to Heaven’s intent, yet are not united in reverent awe, their sentiments will diverge and the Way will not be put into effect. If they assist the Lord on High in establishing his guiding order, yet are not concerted in respectful devotion, indolence will prevail and their work will not be accomplished …

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
必當同其寅畏而典禮之重常若弗能勝協
其恭敬而惇庸之責惟恐罔克盡天命自度君
日嚴於上而臣敬順之也敢以易心乘之乎天
工人代臣寅亮於下而君率作之也敢以怠心
繼之乎夫典禮之在於人即降衷之自乎天者
也君臣之敬畏既同則誠一無間融會流通妙
存神過化之機而五典之克從倫理無不正恩
義無不篤也盡裁成輔相之道而五禮之咸秩
品節無不詳等威無不辨也蓋其惇於我者於
===
其叙於天者無所乖庸於我者於其秩於天者
無所悖民彝物則各得其正而衷無有不和者
矣是則敬畏之心一而後典禮之化行惇庸之
責盡而後安民之效著臯陶陳謨於君之意一
何至與抑衷降於天而民受之以生者也以人
倫則謂之典以尊卑貴賤之品秩則謂之禮其
實非二物也敬不至則衷不和衷不和則典禮
隳而彝倫斁民不可得而安矣此臯陶陳謨之
意而萬世之治法也厥後成湯代夏誕告萬方
punctuated: 必當同其寅畏，而典禮之重常若弗能勝；協其恭敬，而惇庸之責惟恐罔克盡。天命自度，君日嚴於上，而臣敬順之也，敢以易心乘之乎？天工人代，臣寅亮於下，而君率作之也，敢以怠心繼之乎？夫典禮之在於人，即降衷之自乎天者也。君臣之敬畏既同，則誠一無間，融會流通，妙存神過化之機，而五典之克從，倫理無不正，恩義無不篤也；盡裁成輔相之道，而五禮之咸秩，品節無不詳，等威無不辨也。蓋其惇於我者，於其叙於天者無所乖；庸於我者，於其秩於天者無所悖。民彝物則各得其正，而衷無有不和者矣。是則敬畏之心一，而後典禮之化行；惇庸之責盡，而後安民之效著。臯陶陳謨於君之意，一何至與！抑衷降於天，而民受之以生者也。以人倫則謂之典，以尊卑貴賤之品秩則謂之禮，其實非二物也。敬不至則衷不和，衷不和則典禮隳而彝倫斁，民不可得而安矣。此臯陶陳謨之意，而萬世之治法也。厥後成湯代夏，誕告萬方
translation_en:
…They must share the same reverent awe, always feeling as though they cannot bear the weight of the moral norms and rites; they must unite in respectful devotion, fearing only that they cannot fully discharge their responsibility to uphold and put them into practice. Heaven’s mandate is measured by oneself [?]: the ruler daily maintains solemnity above, and his ministers respectfully obey him. Would they dare approach this with a careless heart? Heaven’s work is performed by human agents: ministers reverently assist below, and the ruler leads their efforts. Would he dare follow this with an indolent heart? The moral norms and rites found among human beings are precisely the inward moral nature bestowed by Heaven. Once ruler and ministers share the same reverent awe, their sincerity becomes one, without interruption, blending and circulating freely. Subtly embodying the workings of spiritual presence and transformative influence, they enable the five moral norms to be followed: every human relationship is set right, and affection and righteousness are everywhere deepened. Fully exercising the way of shaping and assisting Heaven’s work, they bring all five rites into order: every ceremonial distinction is fully specified, and every gradation of rank and dignity clearly distinguished. What we uphold thus accords entirely with what Heaven has set in sequence; what we put into practice conflicts in no way with what Heaven has ordered. The constant principles of human life and the standards governing things each attain their proper state, and the inward moral nature is everywhere brought into harmony.

Thus, only after their hearts are united in reverent awe can the transforming influence of moral norms and rites take effect; only after they fully discharge their responsibility to uphold and apply these can the results of bringing peace to the people become manifest. How utterly earnest was Gao Yao’s intention in presenting his counsel to his ruler! Moreover, this inward moral nature descends from Heaven, and the people receive it at birth. In terms of human relationships, it is called moral norms; in terms of the ordered distinctions between higher and lower, noble and humble, it is called rites. In truth, these are not two different things. If reverence is insufficient, the inward moral nature will not be harmonious. If it is not harmonious, moral norms and rites will collapse, the constant human relationships will fall into disorder, and the people cannot be brought peace. This was the intent of Gao Yao’s counsel, and it is the method of government for all ages. Later, when Cheng Tang supplanted the Xia, he proclaimed far and wide to the myriad regions…

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
而降衷綏猷之說蓋本諸此所以成格天之治
追唐虞而匹休之也後世有安民之責者其可
忽焉而不之講哉
王來紹上帝自服于土中旦曰其作大邑
其自時配皇天毖祀于上下其自時中乂
王厥有成命治民今休
楊奬
同考試官教諭陳　批〔此題紹上帝服土中內作者多入敬德講或又分得天得民並講殊悖經旨獨此篇見理〕
===
精到他卷所不逮也
考試官教諭粘　批〔二公作洛心事此作具見寫出老臣惓惓屬望至意可錄〕
考試官教諭劉　批
大臣欲君宅中圖治必證以言而期其效也蓋
宅中以圖治爲急也大臣於此旣引言以證之
而復期其效焉意獨至矣洛邑旣成成王初政
召公作書以達於王至此謂夫洛邑天地之中
而誠民則祈天之本王其自鎬而來定都於斯
奉天以惠民而寵綏之政服於土中皆自天子
punctuated:
而降衷綏猷之說，蓋本諸此，所以成格天之治，追唐虞而匹休之也。後世有安民之責者，其可忽焉而不之講哉？
王來紹上帝，自服于土中。旦曰：「其作大邑，其自時配皇天，毖祀于上下，其自時中乂。」王厥有成命，治民今休。
楊奬
同考試官教諭陳批〔此題紹上帝服土中內，作者多入敬德講，或又分得天得民並講，殊悖經旨。獨此篇見理〕精到，他卷所不逮也。
考試官教諭粘批〔二公作洛心事，此作具見，寫出老臣惓惓屬望至意，可錄〕
考試官教諭劉批
大臣欲君宅中圖治，必證以言而期其效也。蓋宅中以圖治爲急也，大臣於此旣引言以證之，而復期其效焉，意獨至矣。洛邑旣成，成王初政，召公作書以達於王。至此謂夫洛邑天地之中，而誠民則祈天之本。王其自鎬而來，定都於斯，奉天以惠民，而寵綏之政服於土中，皆自天子
translation_en:
…The teaching concerning Heaven’s bestowal of the moral mean and the securing of the proper Way surely derives from this. Through it, Tang achieved a government that reached Heaven, following the rulers of Tang and Yu and matching their excellence. How could those in later ages charged with bringing peace to the people neglect this and fail to study it?
“The king should come here to continue the work of the Lord on High and himself undertake his duties at the center of the land. Dan said: ‘Let him establish this great city; from here let him match August Heaven, carefully conduct sacrifices to the powers above and below, and from here govern from the center.’ The king has received an established mandate; let his government of the people now be excellent.”
Yang Jiang 楊奬
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “In treating ‘continue the work of the Lord on High’ and ‘undertake his duties at the center of the land’ in this topic, most writers introduce a discussion of reverent virtue. Others divide it into winning Heaven and winning the people, discussing both together. These approaches seriously contradict the meaning of the Classic. This essay alone displays a precise and penetrating grasp of the principle, beyond the reach of the other papers.”
Comment by Examiner Nian, Instructor: “This composition fully reveals what the two dukes had in mind in establishing Luo. It expresses the utmost earnestness of an old minister’s hopes for his sovereign. It merits inclusion.”
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor:
When a great minister wishes his sovereign to dwell at the center and pursue good government, he must substantiate his counsel with quoted words and look forward to their effects. Dwelling at the center in order to pursue good government is indeed an urgent task. Here the great minister both quotes words as evidence and looks forward to their effects: his concern is exceptionally profound. When Luoyi had been completed and King Cheng was beginning his rule, the Duke of Shao composed a document to communicate with the king. At this point he says that Luoyi is the center of Heaven and Earth, and that bringing sincerity to the people [?] is the foundation for seeking Heaven’s favor. Let the king come from Hao and establish his capital here, serving Heaven so as to benefit the people. The administration that cherishes and brings them peace is to be carried out at the center of the land, all proceeding from the Son of Heaven…

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
此也相帝以保民而和恒之化弘於新邑惟自
乃御事也間諸旦之言矣作此大邑豈據要會
以爲勝而勤民以自奉哉自是乎履至尊而配
皇天上下神祇王毖祀之自是乎中天下而君
萬邦海宇蒼生王誠和之夫旦之言亦奭之言
也使王允若茲焉庶幾文武誕膺之命弗墜於
天而治民之休赫然於新造之邦矣夏殷迪保
之命常凝於我而宅中之治卓然於守成之世
矣蓋紹帝惟以爲民得乎民斯有以得乎天也
===
誠民所以祈天得乎天斯可以驗乎治也是則
誠民乃新政所先而圖治非宅中不可成王其
知所以疾敬德而亟圖之矣抑召公有陳於王
而重之以周公之言者蓋宅中圖治武王之志
周公知之秩祀裕民之說周公之誥及焉而以
民受命卽周公所謂萬邦咸休惟王有成績者
其說同也論公於人則謀協事擧其效則易從
有周大臣之同心體國忠愛於其君也如此哉
詩
punctuated:
此也。相帝以保民，而和恒之化弘於新邑，惟自乃御事也。間諸旦之言矣：作此大邑，豈據要會以爲勝，而勤民以自奉哉？自是乎履至尊而配皇天，上下神祇，王毖祀之；自是乎中天下而君萬邦，海宇蒼生，王誠和之。夫旦之言，亦奭之言也。使王允若茲焉，庶幾文武誕膺之命弗墜於天，而治民之休赫然於新造之邦矣；夏殷迪保之命常凝於我，而宅中之治卓然於守成之世矣。蓋紹帝惟以爲民，得乎民，斯有以得乎天也；誠民所以祈天，得乎天，斯可以驗乎治也是。則誠民乃新政所先，而圖治非宅中不可。成王其知所以疾敬德而亟圖之矣。抑召公有陳於王，而重之以周公之言者，蓋宅中圖治，武王之志，周公知之；秩祀裕民之說，周公之誥及焉。而以民受命，卽周公所謂萬邦咸休、惟王有成績者，其說同也。論公於人則謀協，事擧其效則易從。有周大臣之同心體國，忠愛於其君也如此哉！

詩
translation_en:
…here. To assist the Lord on High in protecting the people, and to spread the transforming influence of harmony and constancy throughout the new city, depends upon you who administer affairs. Hear [?] the words of Dan: “Was this great city built merely to occupy a strategic gathering place for its advantages, and to toil the people for your own support? From here you will occupy the highest position and become the counterpart of August Heaven: carefully attend to the sacrifices to the spirits above and below. From here you will stand at the center of all under Heaven and rule the myriad states: sincerely bring harmony to the common people throughout the realm.”

Dan’s words are also the words of Shi. If the king truly acts thus, perhaps the Mandate that Kings Wen and Wu so grandly received will not lapse before Heaven, and the blessings of governing the people will shine forth in the newly established state. The Mandate that Xia and Yin followed and preserved will remain firmly with us, and government from the center will stand eminent in an age devoted to preserving the inherited achievement. For carrying on the work of the Lord on High is solely for the people: winning the people provides the means to win Heaven. Treating the people sincerely is the means of seeking Heaven’s favor; winning Heaven’s favor allows the efficacy of government to be verified. Thus sincerity toward the people comes first in a new administration, and establishing good government requires residence at the center. King Cheng should understand how to apply himself diligently to reverencing virtue and urgently undertake this task.

Moreover, the Duke of Shao presented his counsel to the king and reinforced it with the Duke of Zhou’s words because residing at the center to establish good government had been King Wu’s intention, and the Duke of Zhou knew it. The Duke of Zhou’s announcement addressed the orderly performance of sacrifices and the enrichment of the people. Receiving the Mandate through the people is precisely what the Duke of Zhou meant when he said that the myriad states would all enjoy well-being and that the king would have accomplishments: their arguments agree. When deliberations are shared openly with others, counsels accord; when affairs are presented through their effects, they are easy to follow [?]. Such were the great ministers of Zhou in their unity of purpose, their devotion to the state, and their loyalty and affection toward their ruler!

Book of Odes

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
我有嘉賓鼓瑟鼓琴鼓瑟鼓琴和樂且湛
我有旨酒以燕樂嘉賓之心
王命
同考試官訓導路　批〔題本平易場中率多分樂分禮牽强排比作文非是此篇只平平說去而周王燕賓〕
求教之意讀之藹然可掬
同考試官學正程　批〔此題人人類能言之至燕樂嘉賓之心處多不明白惟此篇詞理躍然有周明良相慶〕
===
考試官教諭粘　批〔形容周王欲教示無已之〕
意殆盡
考試官教諭劉　批　文字溫雅
王者自叙燕賓之禮厚而樂賓之意深也蓋所
望於賓者深則所以爲燕者自不容於薄矣周
王求教之誠亦何懇至也哉此燕饗賓客之詩
蓋謂忠告固人臣待用之心而燕饗賓人君待
賢之禮故我有嘉賓弁冕衣裳萃而爲王朝之
彥聲名文物賁而爲上國之光由是和樂以舉
punctuated:
「我有嘉賓，鼓瑟鼓琴。鼓瑟鼓琴，和樂且湛。我有旨酒，以燕樂嘉賓之心。」
王命
同考試官訓導路　批〔題本平易，場中率多分樂分禮，牽强排比作文，非是。此篇只平平說去，而周王燕賓〕求教之意，讀之藹然可掬。
同考試官學正程　批〔此題人人類能言之，至燕樂嘉賓之心處，多不明白。惟此篇詞理躍然，有周明良相慶。〕
考試官教諭粘　批〔形容周王欲教示無已之〕意殆盡。
考試官教諭劉　批：文字溫雅。
王者自叙燕賓之禮厚，而樂賓之意深也。蓋所望於賓者深，則所以爲燕者自不容於薄矣。周王求教之誠，亦何懇至也哉！此燕饗賓客之詩，蓋謂忠告固人臣待用之心，而燕饗賓，人君待賢之禮。故我有嘉賓，弁冕衣裳，萃而爲王朝之彥；聲名文物，賁而爲上國之光。由是和樂以舉
translation_en:
“I have excellent guests; I play the se and qin zithers. I play the se and qin zithers, in harmony and enduring joy. I have fine wine, with which to feast and gladden the hearts of my excellent guests.”

Wang Ming

Comment by Associate Examiner Lu, Assistant Instructor: 〔The topic itself is straightforward. In the examination hall, most candidates separated music from ritual and forced them into parallel arrangements in composing their essays. This is mistaken. This essay simply proceeds in a straightforward manner, yet the Zhou king’s intention in feasting his guests〕 and seeking their instruction comes through with a warmth one can almost grasp.

Comment by Associate Examiner Cheng, Instructor: 〔On this topic, nearly everyone seems able to say something, but most fail to explain clearly the passage about feasting and gladdening the hearts of the excellent guests. Only in this essay do expression and reasoning come vividly to life, showing the enlightened ruler and worthy ministers of Zhou rejoicing together.〕

Comment by Examiner Nian, Instructor: 〔It depicts almost exhaustively the Zhou king’s wish to offer instruction without cease [?]〕.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: The writing is gentle and elegant.

The king himself describes the generosity of the rites with which he feasts his guests and the depth of his intention to give them joy. For when his expectations of his guests are profound, the banquet he provides for them naturally cannot be meager. How earnest and heartfelt, indeed, was the Zhou king’s sincerity in seeking instruction! This is a poem about feasting guests. Its meaning is that loyal counsel is assuredly what ministers wish to offer as they await employment, while feasting guests is the ritual by which a ruler receives worthy men. Thus, I have excellent guests: in their ceremonial caps and robes, they gather as the outstanding men of the royal court; through their renown and cultural accomplishments, they adorn the royal realm with their splendor. Thereupon harmonious music is raised …

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
感燕斯開取瑟而歌則雅韻鏗鏘慶我仁賢之
有遇援琴而鼓則清音流麗樂我邦家之得人
心融於搏拊之餘喜起之情深而自不知適時
之爲久雖雝雝焉和而非暫也神遊於音律之表
明良之誼洽而自不辭永日之爲勞陶陶焉樂
而且久也斯時也琴瑟奏而杯斝行旨酒思柔
羅醴齊於畢陳歌樂和而獻酬舉清酒百壺衍
遠芬於旣載于是而旅飲焉將吾之慇懃而樂
彼之衷曲使猜忌之念消而肝鬲之孚應矣則
===
夫今日之燕豈徒養其體而已耶於是而烝饗
焉達吾之誠敬而結彼之歡心使危疑之慮釋
而腹心之契託矣則夫今日之飲豈徒娛其外
而已耶夫如是則求教之誠庶爲少盡而賓之
教示者將亦無已也吁周之君臣以道相與固
如是夫抑論君之於臣待遇之恩厚則報稱之
義隆今觀有周君以禮待臣而所留者非私惠
臣以道事君而所事者非容悅眞可以媲休都
俞吁咈之盛而致周道興隆之美也後世有召
punctuated: 感燕斯開，取瑟而歌，則雅韻鏗鏘，慶我仁賢之有遇；援琴而鼓，則清音流麗，樂我邦家之得人。心融於搏拊之餘，喜起之情深，而自不知適時之爲久，雖雝雝焉和而非暫也；神遊於音律之表，明良之誼洽，而自不辭永日之爲勞，陶陶焉樂而且久也。斯時也，琴瑟奏而杯斝行，旨酒思柔，羅醴齊於畢陳；歌樂和而獻酬舉，清酒百壺，衍遠芬於旣載。于是而旅飲焉，將吾之慇懃而樂彼之衷曲，使猜忌之念消而肝鬲之孚應矣，則夫今日之燕，豈徒養其體而已耶？於是而烝饗焉，達吾之誠敬而結彼之歡心，使危疑之慮釋而腹心之契託矣，則夫今日之飲，豈徒娛其外而已耶？夫如是，則求教之誠庶爲少盡，而賓之教示者將亦無已也。吁！周之君臣以道相與，固如是夫！抑論君之於臣，待遇之恩厚，則報稱之義隆。今觀有周，君以禮待臣，而所留者非私惠；臣以道事君，而所事者非容悅。眞可以媲休都俞吁咈之盛，而致周道興隆之美也。後世有召
translation_en:
…the banquet thus begins [?]. Taking up the se and singing, we produce elegant, ringing strains, celebrating that our humane and worthy men have found recognition. Drawing near the qin and playing it, we produce clear, flowing tones, rejoicing that our state has gained worthy men. Hearts warm amid the beating of the percussion instruments; so deep is the joy that inspires action that we scarcely notice how long this pleasant time has lasted. Such harmonious concord is no passing thing. Spirits roam beyond the musical notes; the bond between an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers is so close that none complains of the exertion of a whole day. Their abundant joy endures.

At this time, as the qin and se sound and the wine cups circulate, the fine wine is mellow, and the varieties of sweet ritual wine are all set forth. As song and music blend and cups are offered and returned, a hundred jars of clear wine, now fully supplied, spread their fragrance afar. Through drinking together, I convey my solicitude and gladden their innermost hearts, allowing suspicion and jealousy to dissolve and heartfelt trust to find a response. Is today’s banquet, then, merely intended to nourish their bodies? Through feasting together, I communicate my sincerity and reverence and win their affection, allowing apprehension and doubt to fall away and a bond of intimate trust to be established. Is today’s drinking, then, merely intended to give them outward pleasure? In this way, my sincere desire to receive instruction may find some measure of fulfillment, while the instruction offered by my guests will likewise know no end.

Ah! Such indeed was the way ruler and ministers of Zhou associated with one another through the Way! Moreover, in considering a ruler’s relations with his ministers, the greater the kindness with which he treats them, the weightier their obligation to repay it fittingly. Now, looking at Zhou, we see that the ruler treated his ministers according to ritual propriety, and what he bestowed [?] was no private favor; the ministers served their ruler according to the Way, and their service consisted in no ingratiating compliance. This could truly rival the splendid age when ruler and ministers exchanged approval and frank remonstrance, and bring about the glorious flourishing of the Way of Zhou. In later ages, there were those who incurred…

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
譏賦詩好臣其所教而不好臣其所受教此治
之所以終不古若也歟
釐爾女士從以孫子
王儒
同考試官訓導路　批〔詞氣溫純而父兄祝頌其君之意模寫無遺蓋嘗潛玩經傳而有得者〕
同考試官學正程　批〔剗去新冗長之習而歸之溫純典雅之詞三復之餘爲之斂衽〕
考試官教諭粘　批〔深得詩人祝頌之意佳士佳士〕
===
考試官教諭劉　批〔詞豐而意匝〕
詩人述神之福君與之以賢配而繼之以賢偶
也蓋配匹之賢後偶之所由賢也詩人祝君而
致備於是焉忠愛之意何如哉此父兄所以答
行葦也其述尸告之辭曰吾君有天下之尊而
享天下之祿固也然偶焉非賢祿將誰付乎有
賢德之配而生賢德之偶宜也然配非先定偶
安從生哉神於吾君其必念嘉止之有期而默
定乎俔天之配眷元良之攸屬而預綏乎士行
punctuated:
譏賦詩，好臣其所教，而不好臣其所受教，此治之所以終不古若也歟？

釐爾女士，從以孫子。
王儒
同考試官訓導路　批〔詞氣溫純，而父兄祝頌其君之意模寫無遺，蓋嘗潛玩經傳而有得者。〕
同考試官學正程　批〔剗去新冗長之習，而歸之溫純典雅之詞，三復之餘，爲之斂衽。〕
考試官教諭粘　批〔深得詩人祝頌之意，佳士！佳士！〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔詞豐而意匝。〕

詩人述神之福君，與之以賢配，而繼之以賢偶也。蓋配匹之賢，後偶之所由賢也。詩人祝君而致備於是焉，忠愛之意何如哉！此父兄所以答行葦也。其述尸告之辭曰：吾君有天下之尊，而享天下之祿，固也。然偶焉非賢，祿將誰付乎？有賢德之配，而生賢德之偶，宜也。然配非先定，偶安從生哉？神於吾君，其必念嘉止之有期，而默定乎俔天之配；眷元良之攸屬，而預綏乎士行
translation_en:
…incurred criticism in the recitation of poetry [?]: they preferred to take as ministers those whom they taught, rather than those from whom they received instruction. Is this why their government ultimately never equaled that of antiquity?

“He grants you a virtuous lady, and follows this with sons and grandsons.”
Wang Ru

Associate Examiner Lu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The language and tone are gentle and pure, fully portraying the intent of the fathers and elder brothers in blessing and praising their ruler. The author has evidently studied the Classics and their commentaries intently and gained insight from them.”

Associate Examiner Cheng, Instructor, comments: “He strips away the recent habit of prolixity [?], returning to language that is gentle, pure, refined, and elegant. After reading it three times, I straighten my robes in respect.”

Examiner Nian, Instructor, comments: “He deeply grasps the poet’s intent in offering blessings and praise. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!”

Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “The language is abundant and the meaning comprehensive.”

The poet recounts how the spirits bless the ruler, granting him a worthy consort and then worthy successors. For the worthiness of his consort is the source of the worthiness of his descendants. In blessing the ruler, the poet makes his wishes complete in this respect. How profound is his loyal affection! This is how the fathers and elder brothers respond to “The Reeds” (Xing Wei). He recounts the words proclaimed by the personator of the ancestral spirit:

“Our ruler possesses the most exalted position under Heaven and enjoys the emoluments of all under Heaven: this is assuredly fitting. But if his successor is unworthy, to whom will these emoluments be entrusted? That a consort of worthy virtue should bear a successor of worthy virtue is fitting. Yet if the consort is not first chosen, whence can the successor be born? In their concern for our ruler, the spirits will surely remember that the auspicious union has its appointed time and silently determine his consort, the counterpart of Heaven. Mindful of the one upon whom the succession of the foremost worthy depends, they will secure in advance her conduct befitting a noble lady…

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
攝女位正中宮非徒饋食之脩也故而能和足
以配至尊而奉神靈之統思齊之懿範此其承
之焉母儀天下非但象服之宜也貞而且淑足
以相君子而理萬物之宜窈窕之徽音此其紹
之焉夫賢配既釐則所以生賢者有其地矣將
見和氣攸鍾簞筦叶熊羆之吉貞元斯會天潢
呈派矣之祥本之以思齊之懿行而爲敬止之
傳其母既賢其子亦賢矣萬載蒼姬之籙其永
承夫景命之休乎始之以窈窕之規繹而爲孝
===
思之訓其子既賢其孫又賢也萬年豊鎬之區
其永綏夫天祓之祿乎噫父兄祝君福祿而獨
以是爲言亦可謂周於忠愛者矣大抵子孫固
主鬯之托而宮闈實王化之基周自太王姜女
以來嗣續之賢固難指屈而太任太姒姜后之
助尤有不可誣者是詩所陳雖爲一時報答之
辭其亦有見於此與然其所以致是者豈徒然
哉行葦之詩曰以引以翼以享壽祺以介景福
則當時之所以望其臣者驟可見矣君臣一德
punctuated: 攝女位，正中宮，非徒饋食之脩也。故而能和，足以配至尊而奉神靈之統，思齊之懿範，此其承之焉。母儀天下，非但象服之宜也。貞而且淑，足以相君子而理萬物之宜，窈窕之徽音，此其紹之焉。夫賢配既釐，則所以生賢者有其地矣。將見和氣攸鍾，簞筦叶熊羆之吉；貞元斯會，天潢呈派矣之祥。本之以思齊之懿行，而爲敬止之傳，其母既賢，其子亦賢矣。萬載蒼姬之籙，其永承夫景命之休乎！始之以窈窕之規，繹而爲孝思之訓，其子既賢，其孫又賢也。萬年豊鎬之區，其永綏夫天祓之祿乎！噫！父兄祝君福祿，而獨以是爲言，亦可謂周於忠愛者矣。大抵子孫固主鬯之托，而宮闈實王化之基。周自太王姜女以來，嗣續之賢固難指屈，而太任、太姒、姜后之助，尤有不可誣者。是詩所陳，雖爲一時報答之辭，其亦有見於此與？然其所以致是者，豈徒然哉？《行葦》之詩曰：「以引以翼，以享壽祺，以介景福。」則當時之所以望其臣者，驟可見矣。君臣一德
translation_en:
…She assumes the woman's station and takes her rightful place in the central palace; this is more than attending to sacrificial meals. Being thus capable of harmony [?], she is worthy to be consort to the supremely honored ruler and to uphold the succession in serving the spirits. Here she carries forward the admirable example celebrated in “Si Qi” (“Thinking of the Dignified Lady”). As a motherly exemplar to all under Heaven, she does more than fittingly wear ceremonial robes. Steadfast and virtuous, she can assist her lord and bring all things into their proper order. Here she perpetuates the fine reputation of the “gentle and graceful” lady.

Once a worthy consort has been appointed, there is a foundation for bringing forth worthy offspring. We shall see harmonious influences gather: the sleeping mats will accord with the auspicious omen of bears, foretelling sons. The cycle of completion and renewal will converge, and the royal lineage will display auspicious signs of branching descendants [?]. Rooted in the admirable conduct celebrated in “Si Qi,” this will become a tradition of abiding reverence. The mother being worthy, her son will also be worthy. Will not the dynastic destiny of the Ji house endure for myriad ages, forever receiving the blessings of the great Mandate? Beginning with the example of the gentle and graceful lady, this will unfold into instruction in filial devotion. The son being worthy, his son in turn will be worthy. Will not the lands of Feng and Hao endure for ten thousand years, forever enjoying Heaven's blessings [?]?

Ah! When the fathers and elder brothers wish their ruler blessings and prosperity, they speak specifically of this. Their loyalty and love may indeed be called all-embracing. Generally speaking, descendants are certainly those entrusted with presiding over the sacrificial wine, yet the inner palace is truly the foundation of kingly transformation. From King Tai and the lady of the Jiang clan onward, Zhou's worthy successors have been too numerous to count on one's fingers; and the assistance given by Tai Ren, Tai Si, and Queen Jiang is especially undeniable. Although what this poem sets forth was a response offered on a particular occasion, did it not also show an understanding of this principle? Yet could the means by which such results were achieved have been without cause? The poem “Xing Wei” (“The Reeds Along the Path”) says: “To guide and to aid him, that he may enjoy longevity and good fortune, and that great blessings may be increased.” From this we can readily see what the ruler of that time expected of his ministers. Ruler and ministers were united in virtue…
