text:
曰精一曰建中曰建極既極其純故其爲
法曰典則曰人紀曰謨訓自極其備而中
興之盛獨以商高宗首稱者豈非以殷武
說命所稱如不僭不濫憲天聰明有以仰
承乎成湯之法納誨輔德學于古訓有以
允協乎成湯之道視之仲康有侃侯之征
而不能遏后羿之横宣王有蠻荆之伐而
不能免鴻鴈之譏其治爲獨盛乎三代尚
矣胡元竊據華夏腥膻生民之亂極矣我
===
太祖高皇帝不階一旅仗劒北驅有以掃宇宙
所未有之昏霾復帝王所自立之天下其
創大業也視禹湯文武爲最正而其功爲
最大
列聖嗣興繼繼承承恢弘一代之治化藻繪萬
載之太平其所以守大業者視啓大甲成
王爲最賢而其治爲最盛蓋其存諸心者
一精一建中建極之懿施於外者一典則
人紀謨訓之餘大豈偶然之故哉□□□
punctuated:
曰精一，曰建中，曰建極，既極其純，故其爲法，曰典則，曰人紀，曰謨訓，自極其備。而中興之盛，獨以商高宗首稱者，豈非以《殷武》《說命》所稱，如不僭不濫、憲天聰明，有以仰承乎成湯之法；納誨輔德、學于古訓，有以允協乎成湯之道？視之仲康有侃侯之征，而不能遏后羿之横；宣王有蠻荆之伐，而不能免《鴻鴈》之譏，其治爲獨盛乎？三代尚矣，胡元竊據華夏，腥膻生民之亂極矣。
我太祖高皇帝不階一旅，仗劒北驅，有以掃宇宙所未有之昏霾，復帝王所自立之天下。其創大業也，視禹湯文武爲最正，而其功爲最大。
列聖嗣興，繼繼承承，恢弘一代之治化，藻繪萬載之太平。其所以守大業者，視啓大甲成王爲最賢，而其治爲最盛。蓋其存諸心者，一精一建中建極之懿；施於外者，一典則人紀謨訓之餘大。豈偶然之故哉？□□□
translation_en:
…called refinement and singleness of purpose, establishing the mean, and establishing the supreme standard: these had already attained the utmost purity. Thus their governing models—canons and rules, the ordering of human relations, and counsels and instructions—naturally attained complete comprehensiveness. Yet among flourishing restorations, why is that of Gaozong of Shang alone ranked foremost? Was it not because, as celebrated in Martial Shang (Yin wu) and the Charge to Yue (Yue ming), his neither misapplying nor excessively imposing rewards and punishments, and his emulating Heaven’s perceptiveness, enabled him reverently to uphold the laws of Cheng Tang; while his accepting admonition to assist his virtue and studying ancient teachings enabled him truly to accord with Cheng Tang’s Way? Compare him with Zhongkang, who had the expedition of the Lord of Kan [?] yet could not restrain Hou Yi’s tyranny, or King Xuan, who campaigned against the Man and Jing yet could not escape the criticism expressed in Wild Geese (Hong yan). Was Gaozong’s government not uniquely flourishing? The Three Dynasties are remote antiquity. The barbarian Yuan usurped the Chinese realm, and the disorder that befouled the people with its rank stench reached its utmost extreme.
Our Emperor Taizu Gao, without relying even on a single brigade, took up his sword and drove northward. He swept away a darkness unprecedented in the universe and restored the realm established by the sage emperors and kings. In founding his great enterprise, his legitimacy surpassed even that of Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, and his achievement was the greatest.
The successive sage emperors arose in turn, continuing and inheriting the succession, expanding the dynasty’s government and transforming influence, and adorning an age of peace to last ten thousand years. In preserving the great enterprise, they surpassed Qi, Tai Jia, and King Cheng in worthiness, and their government was the most flourishing. What they cherished in their hearts was wholly the excellence of refinement and singleness of purpose [?], establishing the mean, and establishing the supreme standard; what they put into outward practice was wholly the enduring greatness [?] of canons and rules, the ordering of human relations, and counsels and instructions. Could this possibly have come about by chance? [Three illegible characters]…

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝所著祖訓如持守如謹出入如嚴
祭祀如慎國政如禮儀法律内令内官諸
條則皆有合乎殷武說命之旨而持守以
下四篇則於今日爲要也
太宗文皇帝之文華寶鑑聖學心法
仁宗昭皇帝之周易大義
宣宗章皇帝之豳風圖長詠
英宗睿皇帝之日講二典三謨則皆備述乎脩
身齊家之旨而與
===
祖訓法制内令諸條以謹内治重親親者相發
明也我
皇上奮起潛藩入繼大統思
祖宗創守之艱難首任中興治平之責追商宗
恭默之盛美特建嘉靖紀元之號則夫正
治本答群情以弘曠古之觀宜奚先哉竊
亦以爲不過近取
祖宗之舊章遠法商宗之成訓以致其交脩之
力而已如
punctuated:
太祖高皇帝所著《祖訓》，如持守，如謹出入，如嚴祭祀，如慎國政，如禮儀、法律、内令、内官諸條，則皆有合乎《殷武》《說命》之旨，而持守以下四篇，則於今日爲要也。太宗文皇帝之《文華寶鑑》《聖學心法》，仁宗昭皇帝之《周易大義》，宣宗章皇帝之《豳風圖長詠》，英宗睿皇帝之日講《二典》《三謨》，則皆備述乎脩身齊家之旨，而與《祖訓》法制、内令諸條，以謹内治、重親親者相發明也。
我皇上奮起潛藩，入繼大統，思祖宗創守之艱難，首任中興治平之責，追商宗恭默之盛美，特建嘉靖紀元之號。則夫正治本、答群情，以弘曠古之觀，宜奚先哉？竊亦以爲不過近取祖宗之舊章，遠法商宗之成訓，以致其交脩之力而已。如
translation_en:
The Ancestral Instructions compiled by Emperor Taizu Gao contain sections on maintaining what has been inherited, exercising caution in going out and coming in, conducting sacrifices with strict reverence, attending carefully to affairs of state, and such matters as ritual etiquette, laws, inner-palace ordinances, and palace eunuchs. All accord with the purport of “Martial Yin” and “The Charge to Yue.” The four chapters beginning with “Maintaining What Has Been Inherited” are especially essential today. Emperor Taizong Wen’s Precious Mirror of Literary Splendor and Essentials of the Learning of the Sages; Emperor Renzong Zhao’s Great Meaning of the Changes of Zhou; Emperor Xuanzong Zhang’s Extended Verses on Illustrations of the Airs of Bin; and Emperor Yingzong Rui’s daily lectures on the Two Canons and Three Counsels all fully expound the principles of cultivating oneself and ordering one’s family. They mutually illuminate the sections on legal institutions and inner-palace ordinances in the Ancestral Instructions, which call for careful governance within the palace and due regard for affection toward one’s kin.
Our Emperor rose vigorously from his princely fief and entered upon succession to the imperial throne. Reflecting on the difficulties his ancestors faced in founding and preserving their achievement, he made it his foremost responsibility to restore the dynasty and bring orderly and peaceful government. Emulating the splendid example of the Shang ancestral sovereign’s reverent silence, he expressly established “Jiajing” as the designation of his reign era. What, then, should take priority in rectifying the foundations of government and answering the expectations of all, so as to magnify this spectacle unparalleled in antiquity? I humbly believe that it requires no more than drawing upon the established institutions of his own ancestors in the nearer past and taking as models the settled instructions of the Shang ancestral sovereign in the distant past, thereby bringing their mutually reinforcing power of cultivation fully to bear. For example …

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
祖訓至要於今日者曰持守也則近狎必絕偏
聽必察而幷法乎商宗啓寵納侮之訓可
乎曰謹出入也則服用必審星象必占而
幷法乎商宗動惟厥時之訓可乎曰嚴祭
祀也則郊廟必謹百神必恭而幷法乎商
宗黷于祭祀之訓可乎曰慎國政也則耳
目必廣下情必通而幷法乎商宗從諫則
聖之訓可乎至於仰
列聖之規則必讀文華寶鑑而思允執厥中之
===
傳讀聖學心法而戒申韓黃老之術讀周
易大義而幷究十翼之微旨讀豳風圖長
詠而因思王業之艱難講二典三謨而思
治天下之大經大法如商宗之遜志時敏
而道積厥躬終始典學而德脩罔覺可乎
如是則治有光乎創守德無慚於恭默
祖宗所貽之道之法與日月同其光明所傳之
業與天地同其悠久矣正治本答群情者
孰有大於此哉雖然與
punctuated: 祖訓至要於今日者，曰持守也，則近狎必絕，偏聽必察，而幷法乎商宗啓寵納侮之訓，可乎？曰謹出入也，則服用必審，星象必占，而幷法乎商宗動惟厥時之訓，可乎？曰嚴祭祀也，則郊廟必謹，百神必恭，而幷法乎商宗黷于祭祀之訓，可乎？曰慎國政也，則耳目必廣，下情必通，而幷法乎商宗從諫則聖之訓，可乎？至於仰列聖之規，則必讀《文華寶鑑》而思允執厥中之傳，讀《聖學心法》而戒申韓黃老之術，讀《周易大義》而幷究十翼之微旨，讀《豳風圖》長詠而因思王業之艱難，講二典三謨而思治天下之大經大法，如商宗之遜志時敏而道積厥躬，終始典學而德脩罔覺，可乎？如是，則治有光乎創守，德無慚於恭默。祖宗所貽之道之法，與日月同其光明；所傳之業，與天地同其悠久矣。正治本、答群情者，孰有大於此哉？雖然，與
translation_en:
…among the ancestral instructions most essential today is that of maintaining steadfast self-command. Intimate familiarity with favorites must therefore be ended, and one-sided reports carefully scrutinized. Would it not be fitting also to follow the instruction associated with the Shang king Gaozong that granting favor invites disrespect? Another is to exercise care in going out and coming in. Clothing and articles of use must therefore be carefully examined, and celestial signs consulted. Would it not be fitting also to follow Gaozong’s instruction to act only at the proper time? Another is to treat sacrifices with solemnity. The suburban sacrifices and ancestral temple rites must therefore be conducted carefully, and the hundred spirits served reverently. Would it not be fitting also to follow Gaozong’s warning against irreverence in sacrifice? Another is to exercise caution in affairs of state. The channels through which the ruler hears and sees must therefore be broadened, and the circumstances of those below made known. Would it not be fitting also to follow Gaozong’s instruction that accepting remonstrance makes one a sage?

As for looking up to the precedents of the successive sage emperors, one must read the Precious Mirror of Literary Splendor (Wenhua baojian) and reflect on the transmitted teaching to hold faithfully to the Mean; read the Essentials of the Mind in Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa) and guard against the methods of Shen Buhai and Han Fei, and of Huangdi and Laozi; read the Great Meaning of the Changes of Zhou (Zhouyi dayi) and also investigate the subtle purport of the Ten Wings; read the Illustrations of the Airs of Bin (Binfeng tu), chanting at length and thereby reflecting on the hardships of establishing royal rule; and study the Two Canons and Three Counsels, reflecting on the great principles and methods for governing all under Heaven. Would it not be fitting to emulate Gaozong, making one’s purpose humble and continually applying oneself, so that the Way accumulates within one’s person, and always taking learning as one’s constant guide, so that virtue develops imperceptibly?

In this way, your government would bring glory to the founding and preservation of the dynasty, and your virtue would stand without shame beside Gaozong’s reverent silence. The Way and the methods bequeathed by your ancestors would share the radiance of the sun and moon, and the imperial enterprise they transmitted would endure as long as Heaven and Earth. What could be greater than this for rectifying the foundation of government and answering the expectations of all? Nevertheless, to join in [?]…

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
祖宗之治在乎法行
祖宗之法在乎道體
祖宗之道本於心蓋心者治之本而道與法之
寓也人惟此心之存則擇之必精守之必
固行之必力施之必當所體皆正法自無
愆忘之失所慕皆正道自無邪慝之干矣
蓋嘗伏聞我
太祖高皇帝祖訓録成謂侍臣曰一代定法不
可輕改故荒墜厥緒幾於亡夏顛覆典刑
===
幾於亡商又嘗伏聞
宣宗章皇帝讀夢卜求賢之篇謂侍臣曰有高
宗之心然後可以求賢有傳說之賢然後
可以爲相若文帝以夢得鄧通光武以讖
用王梁豈不誤哉大哉王言乎一哉王心
乎今日欲承佑啓之訓踵夢卜之求其又
莊誦
祖宗二言以爲正心之箴可乎謹對
第二問
punctuated:
祖宗之治在乎法行，祖宗之法在乎道體，祖宗之道本於心。蓋心者，治之本而道與法之寓也。人惟此心之存，則擇之必精，守之必固，行之必力，施之必當。所體皆正法，自無愆忘之失；所慕皆正道，自無邪慝之干矣。蓋嘗伏聞我太祖高皇帝《祖訓録》成，謂侍臣曰：「一代定法，不可輕改。」故荒墜厥緒，幾於亡夏；顛覆典刑，幾於亡商。又嘗伏聞宣宗章皇帝讀夢卜求賢之篇，謂侍臣曰：「有高宗之心，然後可以求賢；有傳說之賢，然後可以爲相。若文帝以夢得鄧通，光武以讖用王梁，豈不誤哉？」大哉，王言乎！一哉，王心乎！今日欲承佑啓之訓，踵夢卜之求，其又莊誦祖宗二言，以爲正心之箴，可乎？謹對。

第二問
translation_en:
… The governance of the imperial ancestors depends upon putting their laws into practice; their laws depend upon embodying the Way; and their Way is rooted in the heart. For the heart is the foundation of governance and the dwelling place of the Way and the laws. Only by preserving this heart can one choose with discernment, hold fast with firmness, act with vigor, and apply things appropriately. When all that one embodies is correct law, there will naturally be no errors of transgression or neglect; when all that one reveres is the correct Way, there will naturally be no intrusion of wickedness.

I have humbly heard that, when the Record of Ancestral Instructions was completed, our Emperor Taizu Gao said to his attendant officials: “The established laws of a dynasty must not be lightly altered.” Thus, letting the inherited undertaking fall into neglect brought Xia close to ruin; overturning established statutes brought Shang close to ruin. I have also humbly heard that Emperor Xuanzong Zhang, upon reading the chapter concerning the search for a worthy man through dreams and divination, said to his attendant officials: “Only with a heart like Gaozong’s can one seek worthy men; only with worthiness like Fu Yue’s [the transcription reads 傳說, apparently for 傅說] can one serve as chief minister. When Emperor Wen obtained Deng Tong through a dream, and Guangwu employed Wang Liang on the strength of a prophecy, were these not mistakes?” How great were these royal words! How single-minded were these royal hearts!

Today, if Your Majesty wishes to carry forward their instructions for guiding and aiding posterity, and to follow their search for worthy men through dreams and divination, might Your Majesty solemnly recite these two pronouncements of the imperial ancestors and take them as admonitions for rectifying the heart? I respectfully submit this reply.

Second Question

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
楊諟
同考試官教諭陳 批〔性學極難言此以善與敬發之無餘藴矣〕
考試官教諭粘 批〔辨吾道異端之分極其精切〕
考試官教諭劉 批〔性學類能言之而鮮有真見此篇獨能發程朱未盡之藴非有卓識者不能〕
君子之論性也善而已矣其爲學也敬而
已矣夫性也者合理與氣言之也氣禀不
同而理則一然氣禀可學而變也故曰善
===
學也者所以復性也遏人欲而存天理動
靜交養之功也故曰敬知善與敬則聖賢
所論性學舉不出此而亦可以辨異端之
非矣執事以性學爲問非愚生之所及也
姑述所聞以求質焉夫人之生也得天地
之氣以成形理亦賦焉氣質有清濁厚薄
之不同而理則同合理與氣性之全體理
其本也然必附於氣也氣質雖不可不謂
之性而不可以名性此孔子所以謂之相
punctuated:
楊諟

同考試官教諭陳 批〔性學極難言，此以善與敬發之，無餘藴矣。〕

考試官教諭粘 批〔辨吾道異端之分，極其精切。〕

考試官教諭劉 批〔性學類能言之，而鮮有真見。此篇獨能發程朱未盡之藴，非有卓識者不能。〕

君子之論性也，善而已矣；其爲學也，敬而已矣。夫性也者，合理與氣言之也。氣禀不同，而理則一；然氣禀可學而變也，故曰善。學也者，所以復性也。遏人欲而存天理，動靜交養之功也，故曰敬。知善與敬，則聖賢所論性學，舉不出此，而亦可以辨異端之非矣。執事以性學爲問，非愚生之所及也，姑述所聞以求質焉。夫人之生也，得天地之氣以成形，理亦賦焉。氣質有清濁厚薄之不同，而理則同。合理與氣，性之全體；理其本也，然必附於氣也。氣質雖不可不謂之性，而不可以名性。此孔子所以謂之相
translation_en:
Yang Shi

Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “Human nature and learning are exceedingly difficult to discuss. This essay elucidates them through goodness and reverent attentiveness, leaving none of their implications unexplored.”

Examiner Nian, Instructor, comments: “The distinction between our Way and heterodox teachings is drawn with the utmost precision and pertinence.”

Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “Most can speak about human nature and learning, but few possess genuine insight. This essay alone brings out implications that Cheng and Zhu did not fully expound. Only someone of outstanding discernment could accomplish this.”

When the gentleman discusses human nature, it comes down to goodness alone; when he pursues learning, it comes down to reverent attentiveness alone. Human nature is spoken of in terms of principle and material force taken together. Endowments of material force differ, but principle is one. Yet these endowments can be transformed through learning; hence we speak of goodness. Learning is the means of restoring one's nature. Restraining human desires and preserving Heaven's principle constitute the work of mutual cultivation in activity and stillness; hence we speak of reverent attentiveness. If one understands goodness and reverent attentiveness, then everything the sages and worthies have said about human nature and learning falls within these terms, and one can also distinguish the errors of heterodox teachings. You, honored examiners, have posed a question about human nature and learning, a subject beyond the reach of this humble student. I shall nevertheless relate what I have heard, seeking your correction.

When human beings are born, they receive the material force of Heaven and Earth to constitute their bodily form, and principle is also endowed in them. Their material constitutions differ in clarity and turbidity, richness and thinness, but principle is the same. Principle and material force together constitute human nature in its entirety. Principle is its foundation, yet it must reside in material force. Although one's material constitution must be called part of one's nature, it cannot serve to define nature. This is why Confucius spoke of human natures as mutually …

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
近子思謂之天命而孟子謂之性善善者
窮源極本之論也有生之後情斯動焉情
動則有邪正善惡之不同而性則同合性
與情斯謂之道靜其體也動其用也動於
情而發於善者則道之所由克故子思謂
之致曲孟子謂之擴充朱子釋明明德曰
因所發而遂明之且以敬爲聖學始終之
要也則易言窮理盡性書言危微精一詩
言秉彝好德之說皆可知矣孔子之罕言
===
性以學之未至不可驟語孟子之言性善
則因告子以氣質名性而不可不辨之耳
程子言性之才以兼乎氣質故爲密陸氏
論學則專主於尊德性而不知有氣質之
雜故爲差若佛老之亂性蓋以忘情見性
之說乎愚未嘗深究其書有不能盡知者
然程子嘗曰道之不明異端害之也昔之
害近而易知今之害深而難辨昔之入人
也因其迷暗今之入人也因其高明自謂
punctuated: 近。子思謂之天命，而孟子謂之性善。善者，窮源極本之論也。有生之後，情斯動焉。情動則有邪正善惡之不同，而性則同。合性與情，斯謂之道。靜其體也，動其用也。動於情而發於善者，則道之所由克。故子思謂之致曲，孟子謂之擴充。朱子釋明明德曰：「因所發而遂明之。」且以敬爲聖學始終之要也。則《易》言窮理盡性，《書》言危微精一，《詩》言秉彝好德之說，皆可知矣。孔子之罕言性，以學之未至，不可驟語；孟子之言性善，則因告子以氣質名性，而不可不辨之耳。程子言性之才，以兼乎氣質，故爲密；陸氏論學，則專主於尊德性，而不知有氣質之雜，故爲差。若佛老之亂性，蓋以忘情見性之說乎？愚未嘗深究其書，有不能盡知者。然程子嘗曰：「道之不明，異端害之也。昔之害近而易知，今之害深而難辨。昔之入人也，因其迷暗；今之入人也，因其高明。」自謂
translation_en:
…close to one another. Zisi called it Heaven’s mandate, while Mengzi spoke of human nature as good. To speak of its goodness is to trace it to its source and reach its ultimate foundation. Once life begins, the feelings become active. When feelings stir, they differ in being deviant or correct, good or evil; human nature, however, remains the same. Nature and feelings together constitute what is called the Way. Stillness is its substance; activity is its functioning. When feelings stir and issue in goodness, this is how the Way is fulfilled [?]. Thus Zisi spoke of fully developing a particular aspect of goodness, and Mengzi of extending and filling out goodness. Explaining “making bright one’s bright virtue,” Zhuzi said: “Follow what has manifested itself and thereby fully illuminate it.” He also regarded reverent attentiveness as essential to the learning of the sages from beginning to end. Thus we can understand the statements in the Changes about fathoming principle and fully realizing one’s nature, in the Documents about peril and subtlety, refinement and singleness, and in the Odes about holding fast to the constant nature and loving virtue.

Kongzi seldom spoke of human nature because those whose learning had not yet reached the requisite level could not be told of it precipitately. Mengzi spoke of human nature as good because Gaozi had defined nature in terms of one’s material constitution, making it necessary to distinguish the two. Master Cheng’s discussion of the capacities of human nature encompassed the material constitution and was therefore thorough. Master Lu’s discussion of learning, however, concentrated exclusively on honoring the moral nature, without recognizing the admixture of the material constitution, and was therefore mistaken. As for the confusion about human nature caused by Buddhism and Daoism, does it perhaps arise from their doctrine of forgetting feelings and seeing one’s nature? I have never investigated their writings deeply, and there are matters I cannot fully understand. Yet Master Cheng once said: “That the Way is not clear is due to the harm done by heterodox teachings. In former times, their harm was near the surface and easy to recognize; today, their harm is deep and difficult to discern. Formerly, they gained entry into people’s minds through their confusion and ignorance; today, they gain entry through their intellectual loftiness and brilliance.” They claim for themselves…

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
之窮神知化而不足以開物成務窮深極
微而不可入堯舜之道則其學之弊有可
知矣韓愈氏以性有三品歐陽脩氏以性
非所先蓋皆以氣質言不知性之本矣而
何以斥異端之非故原道本論之所著不
過闢其迹而不能屈其道孟子曰能言距
楊墨者聖人之徒也則其衛道之功豈可
少哉謝上蔡游定夫楊龜山皆程門高弟
蓋嘗聞性然求之太高則忽於事爲之末
===
是以皆近於禪而亦豈真若異端之爲哉
朱子辨之謹其弊耳論其所造則非韓歐
所及而瑜瑾之瑕亦豈敢曲爲諱也夫古
之學者未嘗知性而趨向造詣之正有暗
合於性焉今之學者不過竊程朱之糟粕
耳而何以望古人哉若夫豪傑之士則不
可以槩論矣執事又以會通之旨似是之
非存省之功體用之學以觀諸生之識此
知性者之所辭讓而愚生何足以及之然
punctuated:
之窮神知化，而不足以開物成務；窮深極微，而不可入堯舜之道，則其學之弊有可知矣。韓愈氏以性有三品，歐陽脩氏以性非所先，蓋皆以氣質言，不知性之本矣，而何以斥異端之非？故《原道》《本論》之所著，不過闢其迹，而不能屈其道。孟子曰：「能言距楊墨者，聖人之徒也。」則其衛道之功，豈可少哉？謝上蔡、游定夫、楊龜山皆程門高弟，蓋嘗聞性，然求之太高，則忽於事爲之末，是以皆近於禪，而亦豈真若異端之爲哉？朱子辨之，謹其弊耳。論其所造，則非韓歐所及，而瑜瑾之瑕，亦豈敢曲爲諱也？

夫古之學者未嘗知性，而趨向造詣之正，有暗合於性焉。今之學者不過竊程朱之糟粕耳，而何以望古人哉？若夫豪傑之士，則不可以槩論矣。執事又以會通之旨、似是之非、存省之功、體用之學，以觀諸生之識。此知性者之所辭讓，而愚生何足以及之？然
translation_en:
…what they themselves call fathoming the spiritual and understanding transformation is insufficient to open up an understanding of things and accomplish affairs; though they probe the depths and reach the subtlest mysteries, they cannot enter the Way of Yao and Shun. The defects of their learning can thus be understood. Han Yu held that human nature has three grades, and Ouyang Xiu held that human nature was not the first matter to address. Both spoke in terms of psychophysical endowment and did not understand the foundation of human nature. How, then, could they refute the errors of heterodox teachings? Thus, what they wrote in Inquiry into the Way (Yuan dao) and On Fundamentals (Ben lun) did no more than attack the outward manifestations of those teachings; it could not defeat their doctrines. Mencius said: “Those who can argue against Yang and Mo are followers of the sages.” How, then, could their service in defending the Way be slighted? Xie Shangcai, You Dingfu, and Yang Guishan were all outstanding disciples of the Cheng school and had received instruction concerning human nature. Yet they sought it on too lofty a plane and consequently neglected the particulars of practical affairs. For this reason, all approached Chan Buddhism. But were their practices really the same as those of the heterodox schools? Master Zhu distinguished their errors merely to guard against the resulting harm. In their attainments, they surpassed anything Han Yu and Ouyang Xiu could achieve; yet how could one dare make excuses to conceal these flaws in fine jade?

The scholars of antiquity did not necessarily understand human nature, yet the correctness of their aims and attainments accorded with it unwittingly. Scholars today merely pilfer the dregs of the learning of the Cheng masters and Master Zhu. How could they hope to match the ancients? As for men of exceptional ability, however, they cannot be judged by such generalizations. You, sir, have further tested the students’ understanding through the purport of comprehensive integration, errors that appear correct, the work of preserving the mind and examining oneself, and the study of substance and function. Even those who understand human nature would modestly decline such a task; how could an ignorant student such as I be equal to it? Yet…

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
前已陳其畧矣敢復質所聞焉孟子曰天
下之言性也則故而已矣故者以利爲本
此雖爲智而發而所論性善之原蓋出於
此程子曰論性不論氣不備論氣不論性
不明二之則不是聖賢言性皆不出於此
乎程子曰佛氏敬以直內則有之矣義以
方外則未也然敬以直內亦不是朱子曰
敬有死活只主一敬遇事不濟之以義則
不活吾道異端之辨其在於此乎夫佛老
===
之論性也皆以知覺而論學也皆以靜虛
此與吾之所謂善與敬者何以異哉而似
是之非正在於此夫持靜之久則心體虛
明此吾致知之地而彼遂以爲頓悟其能
應變則亦襲取而已而豈泛應曲當者哉
故必闢之而後可以入道夫古之論性未
嘗分理氣也而其說始於程子蓋不分理
氣則無所指而不明古之言學未嘗分動
靜也而其說始於周子蓋不分動靜則體
punctuated:
前已陳其畧矣，敢復質所聞焉。孟子曰：「天下之言性也，則故而已矣。故者，以利爲本。」此雖爲智而發，而所論性善之原，蓋出於此。程子曰：「論性不論氣，不備；論氣不論性，不明；二之則不是。」聖賢言性，皆不出於此乎？程子曰：「佛氏敬以直內，則有之矣；義以方外，則未也。然敬以直內，亦不是。」朱子曰：「敬有死活，只主一敬，遇事不濟之以義，則不活。」吾道異端之辨，其在於此乎？

夫佛老之論性也，皆以知覺；而論學也，皆以靜虛。此與吾之所謂善與敬者，何以異哉？而似是之非，正在於此。夫持靜之久，則心體虛明，此吾致知之地，而彼遂以爲頓悟。其能應變，則亦襲取而已，而豈泛應曲當者哉？故必闢之，而後可以入道。

夫古之論性，未嘗分理氣也，而其說始於程子，蓋不分理氣，則無所指而不明。古之言學，未嘗分動靜也，而其說始於周子，蓋不分動靜，則體
translation_en:
…I have already outlined this above; I venture now to submit what I have learned for your judgment. Mengzi said: “When people throughout the world speak of human nature, they speak simply of its actual tendencies. These tendencies are rooted in its unimpeded course.” Although this statement was prompted by a discussion of wisdom, the basis for his account of the goodness of human nature emerges from it. Master Cheng said: “To discuss nature without discussing material force is incomplete; to discuss material force without discussing nature is unclear. To treat them as two separate things is wrong.” Do not all the sages’ and worthies’ discussions of nature fall within this account? Master Cheng said: “As for using reverent attentiveness to straighten the inner self, the Buddhists do possess this; as for using righteousness to square outward conduct, they have not attained it. Yet even their straightening of the inner self through reverent attentiveness is not right.” Master Zhu said: “Reverent attentiveness can be dead or alive. If one relies solely on reverent attentiveness and, when confronting affairs, does not supplement it with righteousness, it is not alive.” Does not the distinction between our Way and heterodox teachings lie here?

When Buddhists and Daoists discuss nature, they do so entirely in terms of awareness and perception; when they discuss learning, they do so entirely in terms of stillness and emptiness. How does this differ from what we call goodness and reverent attentiveness? Yet precisely here lies the error that resembles truth. When stillness is maintained for a long time, the substance of the mind becomes empty and luminous. For us, this is the ground upon which to extend knowledge; they, however, take it to constitute sudden enlightenment. Whatever ability they have to respond to changing circumstances is merely borrowed. How could it amount to responding appropriately in every situation and in every particular? Thus their teachings must be refuted before one can enter the Way.

In antiquity, discussions of nature never distinguished principle from material force; this distinction began with Master Cheng. Without distinguishing principle and material force, there would be no definite referent, and the account would remain unclear. In antiquity, discussions of learning never distinguished activity from stillness; this distinction began with Master Zhou. Without distinguishing activity and stillness, substance…

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
用不辨而無所入皆不得已之論理氣夫
豈相離而動靜豈二道哉性雖本善也學
必就其氣質之所近而去其偏學雖主靜
也然必謹於念慮之微而察於事爲之著
故知性之善則聖人之盡性學者之復性
皆此也知學必以敬則靜而存養動而省
察者皆此也敬以直內義以方外以之脩
己則窮理盡性以至於命措諸事業則家
齊國治而天下平然必先知之真而後所
===
向之正是以大學首格物而中庸先於明
善少有毫釐之差鮮不入於異端否則學
術之偏亦足以亂天下管見未知是否執
事其進教焉
第三問
王命
同考試官訓導路　批　敷陳講學納諫非獨考據
精詳寓意遠矣
同考試官學正程　批　說講學納諫處敘事中
punctuated:
用不辨而無所入，皆不得已之論。理氣夫豈相離，而動靜豈二道哉？性雖本善也，學必就其氣質之所近而去其偏；學雖主靜也，然必謹於念慮之微，而察於事爲之著。故知性之善，則聖人之盡性、學者之復性皆此也；知學必以敬，則靜而存養、動而省察者皆此也。敬以直內，義以方外，以之脩己，則窮理盡性以至於命；措諸事業，則家齊國治而天下平。然必先知之真，而後所向之正。是以《大學》首格物，而《中庸》先於明善。少有毫釐之差，鮮不入於異端；否則，學術之偏亦足以亂天下。管見未知是否，執事其進教焉。
第三問
王命
同考試官訓導路批：敷陳講學納諫，非獨考據精詳，寓意遠矣。
同考試官學正程批：說講學納諫處，敘事中
translation_en:
…function would not be distinguished from substance, and there would be no point of entry. These are all distinctions advanced out of necessity. How could principle and material force be separate, and how could activity and stillness constitute two Ways? Although human nature is originally good, learning must address the tendencies of one’s material endowment and remove its biases. Although learning takes stillness as its guiding principle, one must nevertheless be watchful over the subtlest thoughts and attentive to their manifest expression in conduct. Thus, once we understand the goodness of human nature, we see that both the sage’s full realization of that nature and the learner’s recovery of it rest on this. Once we understand that learning must proceed through reverent attentiveness, we see that both preservation and nurture in stillness and examination and scrutiny in activity rest on this. Through reverent attentiveness one makes the inner self upright; through righteousness one makes outward conduct square. Applied to self-cultivation, this means investigating principle fully and realizing one’s nature to the utmost, thereby reaching an understanding of Heaven’s mandate. Applied to practical affairs, it brings order to the family, good government to the state, and peace to all under Heaven. Yet one must first understand truly before one’s course can be correct. This is why the Great Learning begins with the investigation of things, and the Doctrine of the Mean gives priority to understanding goodness. With even the slightest deviation, one seldom avoids falling into heterodox teachings. Even if this does not happen, bias in one’s learning is itself sufficient to throw the realm into disorder. I do not know whether this limited view of mine is correct; may you, honored sir, offer me instruction.
Third Question
Wang Ming 王命
Associate Examiner Lu 路, Assistant Instructor, comments: His exposition of the study and discussion of learning and the acceptance of remonstrance is not merely precise and thorough in its use of evidence; its implications are far-reaching.
Associate Examiner Cheng 程, Instructor, comments: In the passages discussing the study and discussion of learning and the acceptance of remonstrance, within the narration…

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
有議論是作筆
考試官教諭粘　批　諸作止論講學納諫
此篇先以定志擇賢深爲有見文亦典則
考試官教諭劉　批　博洽之學經濟之才忠
懇之意居然可見吾子將來效用幸勿忘斯言
人君莫先於定志志定而擇賢以輔則德
脩而治成矣夫定志者以聖學爲必可至
王道爲必可行不惑於他岐也而又擇賢
以輔則識益明志益正德脩於罔覺矣志
不先定則所向不專所向不專則知人不
明而用賢不篤忠直遠而讒佞進雖强於
講學而久必怠强於納諫而中必違德日
荒而天下無可爲之治也請復明問君心
治之本也講學納諫所以涵養弼直而正
君心也堯舜禹大聖也相傳以執中之學
而交相儆戒湯武反身皆學於師臣而求
言如恐不及傅說之相高宗育以敏學從
諫爲訓唐虞三代之治非偶然矣至周而
punctuated:
有議論，是作筆。

考試官教諭粘批：諸作止論講學納諫，此篇先以定志擇賢，深爲有見，文亦典則。

考試官教諭劉批：博洽之學，經濟之才，忠懇之意，居然可見。吾子將來效用，幸勿忘斯言。

人君莫先於定志，志定而擇賢以輔，則德脩而治成矣。夫定志者，以聖學爲必可至，王道爲必可行，不惑於他岐也。而又擇賢以輔，則識益明，志益正，德脩於罔覺矣。志不先定，則所向不專；所向不專，則知人不明，而用賢不篤，忠直遠而讒佞進。雖强於講學，而久必怠；强於納諫，而中必違。德日荒，而天下無可爲之治也。請復明問：君心，治之本也；講學納諫，所以涵養弼直而正君心也。堯舜禹，大聖也，相傳以執中之學，而交相儆戒。湯武反身，皆學於師臣，而求言如恐不及。傅說之相高宗，育以敏學從諫爲訓。唐虞三代之治，非偶然矣。至周而
translation_en:
…contains reasoned discussion: this is accomplished writing.

Examiner Nian, an Instructor, comments: “The other compositions discuss only the exposition of learning and the acceptance of remonstrance. This essay begins with settling one’s resolve and selecting worthy men, showing considerable insight. Its prose is also dignified and accords with proper standards.”

Examiner Liu, an Instructor, comments: “Broad and thorough learning, talent for governing, and loyal sincerity are plainly evident. When you enter service in the future, I hope you will not forget these words.”

For a ruler, nothing takes precedence over settling his resolve. Once his resolve is settled, if he selects worthy men to assist him, his virtue will be cultivated and good government achieved. Settling one’s resolve means holding that sagely learning can assuredly be attained and the Way of the True King can assuredly be put into practice, without being misled by other paths. If he also selects worthy men to assist him, his discernment will become ever clearer, his resolve ever more upright, and his virtue will be cultivated without his even noticing it. If his resolve is not first settled, his aims will lack focus. If his aims lack focus, he will lack discernment in judging men and steadfastness in employing the worthy: the loyal and upright will be kept at a distance, while slanderers and flatterers advance. Though he exert himself in the exposition of learning, over time he will inevitably grow negligent; though he exert himself in accepting remonstrance, midway he will inevitably turn against it. His virtue will deteriorate daily, and good government will become impossible throughout the realm.

Allow me to return to your illuminating question. The ruler’s heart is the foundation of government. The exposition of learning and the acceptance of remonstrance are the means of nurturing, assisting, and correcting the ruler’s heart, bringing it into rectitude. Yao, Shun, and Yu were great sages. They transmitted to one another the teaching of holding fast to the Mean and admonished and cautioned one another. Tang and Wu examined themselves; both learned from ministers who served as their teachers and sought counsel as though fearing they could not obtain it in time. When Fu Yue served as chief minister to Gaozong, he nurtured him [?], making diligence in learning and compliance with remonstrance his guiding instructions. The good government of Tang and Yu and of the Three Dynasties was no accident. When it came to the Zhou…

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
制官大備師氏以㣲詔王保氏掌諫王惡
公卿至於列士獻詩瞽獻典史獻書師箴
瞍賦矇誦工執藝事以諫近臣進規親戚
補察耆艾脩之其時則太公爲太師周公
爲太傅召公爲太保史佚諸賢相與後先
侍御僕從罔匪正人訓戒如詩書之所稱
不一而足有過則笞伯禽翦桐之戲必諫
是以成王雖以中才而卒成有周之賢王
致刑措之治則周公之教也然成王之思
===
孝繼緒延訪群臣則其志之先定亦不可
誣矣後世英誼之主如漢明帝臨雍拜老
執經問難唐太宗開弘文之館訪問治道
可謂知講學矣漢文帝前席賈生乃訪鬼
神之事宋太宗日覽廣記徒事博物之書
何爲者哉比之荒怠廢政者則有間矣然
五更之尊而得桓榮之陋登瀛之選而列
許敬宗之奸亦豈得爲盡善哉文帝止輦
受言必稱其善唐太宗聽魏徵仁義之說
punctuated:
制官大備，師氏以㣲詔王，保氏掌諫王惡。公卿至於列士獻詩，瞽獻典，史獻書，師箴，瞍賦，矇誦，工執藝事以諫，近臣進規，親戚補察，耆艾脩之。其時則太公爲太師，周公爲太傅，召公爲太保，史佚諸賢相與後先，侍御僕從罔匪正人。訓戒如詩書之所稱，不一而足。有過則笞伯禽，翦桐之戲必諫。是以成王雖以中才，而卒成有周之賢王，致刑措之治，則周公之教也。然成王之思孝繼緒，延訪群臣，則其志之先定亦不可誣矣。
後世英誼之主，如漢明帝臨雍拜老，執經問難；唐太宗開弘文之館，訪問治道，可謂知講學矣。漢文帝前席賈生，乃訪鬼神之事；宋太宗日覽廣記，徒事博物之書，何爲者哉？比之荒怠廢政者則有間矣。然五更之尊而得桓榮之陋，登瀛之選而列許敬宗之奸，亦豈得爲盡善哉？文帝止輦受言，必稱其善；唐太宗聽魏徵仁義之說
translation_en:
…the establishment of offices became fully developed. The Preceptor instructed the king through subtle guidance, while the Protector was charged with remonstrating against the king’s faults. From the dukes and ministers down to the ranked officers, all presented poems; blind musicians presented precedents, scribes presented writings, music masters offered admonitions, sightless musicians recited verses, and blind musicians chanted. Artisans offered remonstrance through the practice of their crafts; close attendants submitted counsel; royal kinsmen remedied omissions and scrutinized faults; and elders refined these efforts. At that time, the Grand Duke served as Grand Preceptor, the Duke of Zhou as Grand Mentor, and the Duke of Shao as Grand Guardian. Scribe Yi and the other worthy men supported the king before and behind; among his attendants and servants there was not one who was not upright. Their instructions and admonitions, as recorded in the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents, were too numerous to enumerate. When the king committed a fault, Boqin was caned; even his jest with a cut tung leaf invariably drew remonstrance. Thus King Cheng, though of middling ability, ultimately became a worthy king of Zhou and achieved a reign in which punishments could be set aside. This was due to the Duke of Zhou’s teaching. Yet King Cheng’s desire to act with filial devotion and carry on his predecessors’ work, and his summoning of ministers for consultation, also show that his resolve was fixed from the outset—a fact that cannot be denied.
Among the outstanding and righteous rulers of later ages, Emperor Ming of Han visited the imperial academy and paid homage to an elder, holding a classic as he questioned him about difficult passages; Emperor Taizong of Tang established the Institute for the Advancement of Literature and inquired into the Way of government. They may be said to have understood the importance of studying and discussing learning. Emperor Wen of Han moved forward on his mat toward Master Jia, only to ask about ghosts and spirits; Emperor Taizong of Song read the Extensive Records daily, merely occupying himself with a book of miscellaneous knowledge. What were they accomplishing? They were certainly different from rulers who indulged in idleness and neglected government. Yet the honored position of Elder of Fivefold Experience was held by someone as limited as Huan Rong, and the selection of scholars likened to ascending the immortal isle of Yingzhou included someone as treacherous as Xu Jingzong. How could these arrangements be called wholly good? Emperor Wen stopped his carriage to receive advice and invariably praised what was good in it; Emperor Taizong of Tang listened to Wei Zheng’s teachings on benevolence and righteousness…

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
行之有效可謂善納諫矣漢武帝賞東方
朔之直諫而卒起上林之役魏文帝納辛
毗引裾之諫而卒徙冀州之半諫何益邪
比之拒諫飾非者則有間矣然治安之策
未行而長沙之謫已遺仁義之效方著而
殺田舍翁之心已萌又安在其能用諫乎
是以數君雖有英誼之資而無正心之實
又無如周公者以輔之是以治之不古若
也程伊川范太史嘗勸哲宗以講學矣伊
===
川之疏曰陛下春秋方富而輔養之道不
可不至一日之中接賢士大夫之時多親
宦官宮妾之時少則氣質變化願選名儒
勸講有過隨事獻箴必能養成聖德范祖
禹曰今日學與不學係他日之治亂好學
則天下君子願立於朝不學則小人皆動
其心以求富貴人主之進學莫不在於少
時數年之後恐不得如今日之學勸講學
者雖多二賢大儒也其論至矣陸贄司馬
punctuated:
行之有效，可謂善納諫矣。漢武帝賞東方朔之直諫，而卒起上林之役；魏文帝納辛毗引裾之諫，而卒徙冀州之半，諫何益邪？比之拒諫飾非者則有間矣，然治安之策未行，而長沙之謫已遺；仁義之效方著，而殺田舍翁之心已萌，又安在其能用諫乎？是以數君雖有英誼之資，而無正心之實，又無如周公者以輔之，是以治之不古若也。
程伊川、范太史嘗勸哲宗以講學矣。伊川之疏曰：「陛下春秋方富，而輔養之道不可不至。一日之中，接賢士大夫之時多，親宦官宮妾之時少，則氣質變化。願選名儒勸講，有過隨事獻箴，必能養成聖德。」范祖禹曰：「今日學與不學，係他日之治亂。好學則天下君子願立於朝，不學則小人皆動其心以求富貴。人主之進學，莫不在於少時；數年之後，恐不得如今日之學。」勸講學者雖多，二賢大儒也，其論至矣。陸贄、司馬
translation_en:
…and put it into practice with effective results: he may be said to have been good at accepting remonstrance. Emperor Wu of Han rewarded Dongfang Shuo for his forthright remonstrance, yet ultimately undertook the construction works at Shanglin. Emperor Wen of Wei accepted Xin Pi’s remonstrance when Xin tugged at his robe, yet ultimately relocated half the population of Jizhou. What benefit did remonstrance bring? These rulers were better than those who rejected remonstrance and concealed their faults. Yet before the proposals for lasting order and security were implemented, banishment to Changsha had already been imposed [?]; just as the effects of benevolence and righteousness were becoming apparent, the desire to kill that “country bumpkin” had already arisen. Where, then, was their ability to act upon remonstrance? Thus, although these rulers possessed outstanding natural gifts, they lacked the actual achievement of rectifying their minds. Nor did they have anyone like the Duke of Zhou to assist them. This is why their governance fell short of that of antiquity.
Cheng Yichuan and Grand Historian Fan once urged Emperor Zhezong to pursue learning through lectures and discussion. Yichuan’s memorial said: “Your Majesty is still young, and the means of guiding and nurturing you must be brought to the utmost perfection. If, during each day, you spend more time meeting worthy scholar-officials and less time in the company of eunuchs and palace women, your temperament will be transformed. I ask that you select eminent Confucian scholars to encourage your learning and expound the texts. Whenever you err, let them offer admonition appropriate to the occasion. This will surely nurture your sagely virtue.” Fan Zuyu said: “Whether you study today determines whether there will be order or disorder in the future. If you love learning, the gentlemen of the realm will wish to serve at court. If you do not study, petty men will all be stirred to seek wealth and rank. A ruler’s advancement in learning must take place while he is young. After several years, I fear you will no longer be able to study as you can today.” Although many have urged rulers to pursue learning through lectures and discussion, these two worthy men were great Confucian scholars, and their arguments were unsurpassed. Lu Zhi and Sima…

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
光昔勸其君以納諫矣贄之言曰人君者
直言則其智益大求過行則其德彌光惟
闇惑之主諱其過行忿其直言以阿諛爲
納忠以諫諍爲揚惡光之言曰君降心以
訪問臣竭誠以獻替則庶政脩治君惡逆
耳之言臣爲便身之計則下情壅蔽勸納
諫者雖多二公賢相也其言切矣惜乎當
時之君俱不能聽也而豈非萬世之鑒哉
夫講學納諫莫先於定志莫要於得賢擇
===
賢之道任相而已矣輔相之任求天下之
賢而已矣拔縉紳之望顯巖穴之幽淵源
醇正者置之侍從忠亮鯁直者列之諫諍
無拘於常格無蔽於浮名而後可以收得
賢之效也勸講之官正己以積誠隨事以
規諷不爲迂踈之談不事文藝之末諫諍
之臣國是必争君過必舉不默默以容不
瑣瑣以瀆然後可以成正君之功也執事
諄諄以古之講學納諫爲問者豈不欲爲
punctuated:
光昔勸其君以納諫矣。贄之言曰：「人君者直言，則其智益大；求過行，則其德彌光。惟闇惑之主，諱其過行，忿其直言，以阿諛爲納忠，以諫諍爲揚惡。」光之言曰：「君降心以訪問，臣竭誠以獻替，則庶政脩治；君惡逆耳之言，臣爲便身之計，則下情壅蔽。」勸納諫者雖多，二公賢相也，其言切矣。惜乎當時之君俱不能聽也，而豈非萬世之鑒哉！
夫講學納諫，莫先於定志，莫要於得賢。擇賢之道，任相而已矣；輔相之任，求天下之賢而已矣。拔縉紳之望，顯巖穴之幽，淵源醇正者置之侍從，忠亮鯁直者列之諫諍。無拘於常格，無蔽於浮名，而後可以收得賢之效也。勸講之官，正己以積誠，隨事以規諷，不爲迂踈之談，不事文藝之末；諫諍之臣，國是必争，君過必舉，不默默以容，不瑣瑣以瀆。然後可以成正君之功也。執事諄諄以古之講學納諫爲問者，豈不欲爲
translation_en:
…Guang formerly urged their rulers to accept remonstrance. Lu Zhi said: “When a ruler [welcomes?] frank speech, his wisdom grows greater; when he seeks out faults in his conduct, his virtue shines ever more brightly. Only a benighted and deluded ruler conceals his faults and resents frank speech, taking flattery as an offering of loyalty and remonstrance as the exposure of his failings.” Sima Guang said: “When the ruler humbles himself to seek advice and his ministers offer their utmost sincerity in recommending what is good and opposing what is wrong, the various affairs of government are well ordered. When the ruler detests words that grate on his ears and his ministers scheme for their own convenience, the circumstances of those below are blocked from his view.” Although many have urged rulers to accept remonstrance, these two men were worthy chief ministers, and their words struck home. Alas, neither ruler of their time could heed them! Is this not a lesson for all ages?
In pursuing learning and accepting remonstrance, nothing takes precedence over fixing one’s resolve, and nothing is more essential than obtaining worthy men. The way to select worthy men lies simply in appointing a chief minister; the chief minister’s responsibility lies simply in seeking worthy men throughout the realm. Promote those held in esteem among the official class, and bring to prominence those living in secluded obscurity. Place men whose intellectual grounding is pure and correct among the court attendants, and appoint the loyal, trustworthy, forthright, and upright to the ranks of remonstrating officials. Only by avoiding the constraints of routine appointment rules and refusing to be blinded by empty reputations can one reap the benefits of obtaining worthy men. Officials charged with encouraging and expounding learning should rectify themselves to deepen their sincerity and offer corrective counsel as occasions arise. They should neither indulge in impractical discourse nor devote themselves to the superficial refinements of literary composition. Remonstrating ministers must contend over the proper direction of state policy and bring every fault of the ruler to his attention. They must neither remain silent to secure acceptance nor weary him with petty complaints. Only then can they succeed in rectifying the ruler. In earnestly asking about the pursuit of learning and acceptance of remonstrance in antiquity, do you not wish to contribute…

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
今日之一助乎竊惟
聖天子春秋鼎盛厲精方切固已諫行言聽而
近日巳
御經筵天下臣民慶幸然猶望以唐虞三代
爲必可師漢唐宋之君爲不足法虛求道
之心廣陳言之路勸講之餘有所規獻俯
賜延納章奏之入雖有狂直無厭聽覽則
社稷幸甚天下幸甚執事與其進也倘獲承對
大庭之末猶將執此
===
獻焉
第四問
何尚德
同考試官教諭陳　批　格天處該博之士類能言之畏天一意非具夫忠愛之實者或未之及焉此作獨得之佳也
考試官教諭粘　批　說上下交脩處隱然有自效之意蓋留心於當世之務者
考試官教諭劉　批　考究斷制俱到非但文字之工也秋闈得子主司寧不自慶
punctuated:
今日之一助乎？竊惟聖天子春秋鼎盛，厲精方切，固已諫行言聽，而近日巳御經筵，天下臣民慶幸。然猶望以唐虞三代爲必可師，漢唐宋之君爲不足法，虛求道之心，廣陳言之路。勸講之餘，有所規獻，俯賜延納；章奏之入，雖有狂直，無厭聽覽，則社稷幸甚，天下幸甚！執事與其進也，倘獲承對大庭之末，猶將執此獻焉。
第四問
何尚德
同考試官教諭陳，批：「格天處，該博之士類能言之；畏天一意，非具夫忠愛之實者，或未之及焉。此作獨得之，佳也。」
考試官教諭粘，批：「說上下交脩處，隱然有自效之意，蓋留心於當世之務者。」
考試官教諭劉，批：「考究、斷制俱到，非但文字之工也。秋闈得子，主司寧不自慶？」
translation_en:
…to be of some assistance in the present day? I humbly reflect that our sagely Son of Heaven is in the prime of life and intensely devoted to diligent government. He already acts upon remonstrances and heeds advice, and recently he has attended the Classics Colloquium, to the rejoicing of officials and common people throughout the realm. Yet we still hope that he will regard the ages of Tang Yao and Yu Shun and the Three Dynasties as models that can assuredly be followed, and the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song as inadequate examples; that he will seek the Way with an open mind and broaden the avenues for presenting advice. When, in addition to their lectures, his lecturers offer admonitions, may he graciously receive and accept them. When memorials arrive, even if their language is rashly outspoken, may he never tire of hearing and reading them. Then how fortunate would be the altars of soil and grain, and how fortunate the whole realm! If you, sir, approve my advancement, and I should gain a place among the last to respond at the imperial court, I shall still present these views there.
Fourth Policy Question
He Shangde
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “On the matter of moving Heaven, broadly learned scholars can generally discourse. But the idea of revering Heaven may escape those who lack genuine loyalty and love for their sovereign. This composition alone grasps it: excellent.”
Examiner Nian, Instructor, comments: “In discussing how those above and below must both cultivate themselves, he implicitly expresses a desire to offer his own service. He is evidently someone who gives thought to the affairs of the present age.”
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “His investigation and judgment are both thorough; this is more than skill in composition alone. Having found you in the autumn Provincial Examination, how could the presiding examiners fail to congratulate themselves?”

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
格天之道固在乎本末之交脩畏天之心
尤貴乎始終之無間蓋克謹天威者君之
責而仁愛人君者天之心也入君德脩於
身固致治之本而一政一事之未脩亦不
可以爲末而忽之也治成而祥興固天之
示應於終甫治而災興亦天之所以示警
於始也然則格天之道固不容以偏廢而
畏天之心又其可以一時而少怠哉請因
明問而陳之書曰惟天無親克敬惟親格
===
天之道也詩曰畏天之威于時保之畏天
之心也故燕及皇天周文以之興王業厥
德靡常尤有以亡夏后以之而自絕於天
相與之幾微矣可不畏哉昔箕子陳洪範
休徵之疇以人之五行驗天之五事所感
之祥各以類應如曰肅時雨若曰又時暘
若曰哲時燠若曰謀時寒若曰聖時風若
其爲人君脩德之勸至矣至漢劉向傳五
行則有謂貌之不肅厥罰恒雨時則有服
punctuated: 格天之道，固在乎本末之交脩；畏天之心，尤貴乎始終之無間。蓋克謹天威者，君之責；而仁愛人君者，天之心也。入君德脩於身，固致治之本，而一政一事之未脩，亦不可以爲末而忽之也。治成而祥興，固天之示應於終；甫治而災興，亦天之所以示警於始也。然則格天之道，固不容以偏廢，而畏天之心，又其可以一時而少怠哉？請因明問而陳之。《書》曰：「惟天無親，克敬惟親。」格天之道也。《詩》曰：「畏天之威，于時保之。」畏天之心也。故「燕及皇天」，周文以之興王業；「厥德靡常，尤有以亡」，夏后以之而自絕於天。相與之幾微矣，可不畏哉？昔箕子陳《洪範》休徵之疇，以人之五行驗天之五事，所感之祥，各以類應。如曰「肅，時雨若」，曰「又，時暘若」，曰「哲，時燠若」，曰「謀，時寒若」，曰「聖，時風若」，其爲人君脩德之勸至矣。至漢劉向傳《五行》，則有謂「貌之不肅，厥罰恒雨，時則有服
translation_en:
The way to move Heaven lies indeed in cultivating both root and branches together; a heart that fears Heaven prizes above all an unbroken constancy from beginning to end. For reverently heeding Heaven’s majesty is the ruler’s responsibility, while benevolent love for the ruler is Heaven’s intention. The ruler’s cultivation of virtue in his own person [?] is certainly the foundation of good government; yet any single policy or affair left unattended must not be dismissed as a mere branch and neglected. When government is perfected and auspicious signs arise, Heaven manifests its response at the end; when government has only just begun and calamities arise, Heaven likewise issues warnings at the beginning. Thus, if the way to move Heaven permits neither aspect to be neglected, how could a heart that fears Heaven allow even a moment’s slight relaxation? Allow me to explain in response to your illuminating question.

The Book of Documents says: “Heaven has no favorites; it favors those capable of reverence.” This is the way to move Heaven. The Book of Odes says: “Fear Heaven’s majesty, and thereby preserve it.” This expresses the heart that fears Heaven. Thus, through conduct whose “peaceful influence reached august Heaven,” King Wen of Zhou established the royal enterprise; through conduct described as “his virtue was inconstant, and he had further cause to perish” [?], the ruler of Xia cut himself off from Heaven. How subtle are the workings of their mutual relations! Can one fail to stand in awe?

Formerly, when Jizi expounded the category of favorable signs in the “Great Plan,” he used the five forms of human conduct to examine Heaven’s five affairs [?]. The auspicious signs elicited corresponded each according to its kind. Thus it says: “Gravity: timely rain accords with it”; “You [?]: timely sunshine accords with it”; “Discernment: timely warmth accords with it”; “Deliberation: timely cold accords with it”; and “Sagacity: timely wind accords with it.” Its encouragement to rulers to cultivate virtue could scarcely be greater. Later, when Liu Xiang of the Han expounded the Five Phases, he said: “When the demeanor lacks gravity, its punishment is incessant rain; then there are clothing …

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
妖龜孼雞禍言之不乂厥罰恒暘時則有
詩妖之類似於洪範有相發明焉然五事
庶徵可條而入而八政五紀之類皆不可
通誠有如蘇洵所譏者惟胡安國則直謂
孔子言春秋而不言事應而事應在其中
蓋以天道雖未嘗或爽而推測則容有未
盡推之而不驗則非惟戾聖經之旨而反
啓人君慢天之心不若不言之爲愈其論
誠得之矣周禮保章氏以九州之星土辨
===
封域之災祥所應之地各以其方如曰玄
枵星紀爲齊與越之分星實沈大火爲晉
與宋之分星娵訾鶉尾爲衛與楚之分星
析木鶉火鶉首爲燕與周秦之分星其爲
人君救政序事之勸詳矣至唐太宗脩晉
天文志則有謂自危至奎爲娵訾爲衛之
分野屬幷州自畢至東井爲實沈爲魏之
分野屬益州之類似於保章氏有合焉然
衛本受封商墟於幷州了不相干魏分晉
punctuated:
妖、龜孼、雞禍；言之不乂，厥罰恒暘，時則有詩妖之類，似於《洪範》有相發明焉。然五事、庶徵可條而入，而八政、五紀之類皆不可通，誠有如蘇洵所譏者。惟胡安國則直謂孔子言《春秋》而不言事應，而事應在其中。蓋以天道雖未嘗或爽，而推測則容有未盡，推之而不驗，則非惟戾聖經之旨，而反啓人君慢天之心，不若不言之爲愈。其論誠得之矣。
《周禮》保章氏以九州之星土辨封域之災祥，所應之地各以其方。如曰玄枵、星紀爲齊與越之分星，實沈、大火爲晉與宋之分星，娵訾、鶉尾爲衛與楚之分星，析木、鶉火、鶉首爲燕與周、秦之分星，其爲人君救政序事之勸詳矣。至唐太宗脩《晉天文志》，則有謂自危至奎爲娵訾，爲衛之分野，屬幷州；自畢至東井爲實沈，爲魏之分野，屬益州之類，似於保章氏有合焉。然衛本受封商墟，於幷州了不相干；魏分晉
translation_en:
…prodigies, turtle abnormalities, and calamities involving chickens; when speech is not orderly, its punishment is constant sunshine, and at such times there are prodigies in verse and the like. These accounts seem to shed light on the “Great Plan” and to be illuminated by it in turn. Yet although the Five Activities and the Various Signs can be classified and fitted into this scheme, categories such as the Eight Affairs of Government and the Five Regulators of Time cannot be reconciled with it. There is indeed substance to Su Xun’s criticism. Hu Anguo, however, stated directly that Confucius expounded the Spring and Autumn Annals without discussing correspondences between events and their portents, yet those correspondences were contained within it. For although the Way of Heaven never errs, attempts to infer its workings may fall short of full understanding. When such inferences fail to be borne out, they not only contradict the purport of the sage’s classic but actually encourage rulers to hold Heaven in contempt. It is better, therefore, to leave such matters unspoken. His argument truly gets the point right.
In the Rites of Zhou, the Astrologer distinguishes calamities and auspicious signs affecting territorial domains through the celestial territories corresponding to the Nine Provinces; each terrestrial region to which a sign applies is determined by its respective direction. Thus, for example, Xuanxiao and Xingji are the celestial divisions assigned to Qi and Yue; Shichen and Dahuo those assigned to Jin and Song; Juzi and Chunwei those assigned to Wei 衛 and Chu; and Ximu, Chunhuo, and Chunshou those assigned to Yan, Zhou, and Qin. This provides detailed encouragement for rulers to remedy their government and put affairs in order. When Emperor Taizong of Tang had the “Treatise on Astronomy” of the History of Jin compiled, it included statements such as these: the stretch from the mansion Wei 危 to Kui constitutes Juzi, the celestial division of Wei 衛, and belongs to Bingzhou; the stretch from Bi to Dongjing constitutes Shichen, the celestial division of Wei 魏, and belongs to Yizhou. Such statements seem to agree with the account of the Astrologer. Yet Wei 衛 was originally enfeoffed at the former site of Shang and had absolutely no connection with Bingzhou; Wei 魏 received a portion of Jin’s…

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
地於益州亦不相屬則誠有如洪邁所譏
者惟鄭樵則直謂古人封國之初命其君
以分主祀事蓋以地有不齊而分野之在
天則不易以不齊之地配不易之分野於
理尤爲難通其論蓋近之也人君誠能脩
五事於已驗五行於天而留神乎庶徵之
訓君救政於上臣叙事於下而詳玩乎吳
澂之言則雨暘燠寒風各以其時二十八
宿各循其度而上天孚佑之心可保其必
隆矣然禎祥之興固在乎感格之有道災
變之至尤貴乎敬畏之常存仰惟我
聖天子因神人之交與應承平之休運
臨御之初首誅左右壅蔽之奸次黜佞靡邪
淫之技蠲逋負革冒濫抑萑豪起遺逸若
無致災之由者而邇來日蝕火災風霾地
震猶未免於屢見何哉愚以爲人君者父
天母地而爲之子者也愛而知勞固父母
愛子之道勞而不怨尤人子敬畏之心故
punctuated:
地，於益州亦不相屬，則誠有如洪邁所譏者。惟鄭樵則直謂古人封國之初，命其君以分主祀事。蓋以地有不齊，而分野之在天則不易，以不齊之地配不易之分野，於理尤爲難通。其論蓋近之也。人君誠能脩五事於已，驗五行於天，而留神乎庶徵之訓；君救政於上，臣叙事於下，而詳玩乎吳澂之言，則雨暘燠寒風各以其時，二十八宿各循其度，而上天孚佑之心可保其必隆矣。然禎祥之興，固在乎感格之有道；災變之至，尤貴乎敬畏之常存。

仰惟我聖天子因神人之交與，應承平之休運，臨御之初，首誅左右壅蔽之奸，次黜佞靡邪淫之技，蠲逋負，革冒濫，抑萑豪，起遺逸，若無致災之由者。而邇來日蝕、火災、風霾、地震，猶未免於屢見，何哉？愚以爲人君者，父天母地而爲之子者也。愛而知勞，固父母愛子之道；勞而不怨，尤人子敬畏之心。故
translation_en:
…territory, and likewise has no territorial connection with Yizhou. Thus there is indeed substance to Hong Mai’s criticism. Zheng Qiao, however, states outright that when the ancients first established the enfeoffed states, they charged their rulers with separately presiding over the respective sacrifices. Territorial boundaries vary, whereas the corresponding celestial divisions remain fixed; matching variable territories to fixed celestial divisions is particularly difficult to justify in principle. His argument probably comes close to the truth. If the ruler can truly cultivate the Five Conducts in himself, examine the workings of the Five Phases in Heaven, and attend carefully to the teaching on the Various Verifications; if the ruler above corrects government and his ministers below set affairs in order, carefully pondering Wu Cheng’s words, then rain, sunshine, warmth, cold, and wind will each arrive in season, and the twenty-eight lunar lodges will each follow their proper courses. We may then be assured that Heaven’s disposition to grant faithful protection will flourish. Yet while the appearance of auspicious signs certainly depends on having the proper means to move Heaven, when calamities and anomalies arrive, it is especially important to maintain constant reverence and awe.

We reverently consider how our sagely Son of Heaven, receiving the joint support of spirits and men and responding to the auspicious fortune of an age of peace, at the beginning of his reign first executed the wicked attendants who obstructed and concealed the truth, and next dismissed those practicing flattering, frivolous, depraved, and licentious arts. He remitted outstanding debts, eliminated fraudulent and excessive claims, restrained powerful brigands [?], and summoned overlooked men of worth to service. It would seem that no cause remained for bringing on calamities. Yet recently solar eclipses, fires, windstorms and dust haze, and earthquakes have continued to recur. Why is this? In my humble view, the ruler takes Heaven as his father and Earth as his mother, and stands as their son. To love a child while knowing to put him to toil is indeed the way parents love their children; to toil without resentment is, above all, the reverent and fearful disposition of a son. Thus …

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
黃龍負舟天之所以儆乎禹也竭力勞民
一言禹之畏天何其至乎七年之旱天之
所以儆乎湯也桑林自責數語湯之敬天
何其至乎若乃庸君昏主皆自絕於天者
天亦厭而棄之矣尚何示戒之有哉伏聞
聖天子每遇災變之臨戰兢惕勵不遑昕夕是
固默知天心之有在而存夫畏天之心矣
然逋負雖蠲而裕財之道未盡舉冒濫雖
革而祈恩之途未盡塞萑豪雖抑而罔利
===
者尚存覬倖之心遺逸雖起而進言者或
蒙擯斥之譴毋乃畏天之心尚有未至而
弭變之道亦未爲盡乎伏願
聖天子執數者之政堅如金石守數者之政信
如四時平數者之政無私如天地不以有
災而敬畏於始不以無災而怠忽於終則
一念畏天之心即大禹竭力勞民之心成
湯桑林請禱之心格天之道亦不外於此
而得之矣又何災變之難弭而至治之難
punctuated: 黃龍負舟，天之所以儆乎禹也。「竭力勞民」一言，禹之畏天何其至乎！七年之旱，天之所以儆乎湯也。桑林自責數語，湯之敬天何其至乎！若乃庸君昏主，皆自絕於天者，天亦厭而棄之矣，尚何示戒之有哉？伏聞聖天子每遇災變之臨，戰兢惕勵，不遑昕夕，是固默知天心之有在，而存夫畏天之心矣。然逋負雖蠲，而裕財之道未盡舉；冒濫雖革，而祈恩之途未盡塞；萑豪雖抑，而罔利者尚存覬倖之心；遺逸雖起，而進言者或蒙擯斥之譴。毋乃畏天之心尚有未至，而弭變之道亦未爲盡乎？伏願聖天子執數者之政，堅如金石；守數者之政，信如四時；平數者之政，無私如天地。不以有災而敬畏於始，不以無災而怠忽於終，則一念畏天之心，即大禹竭力勞民之心、成湯桑林請禱之心，格天之道亦不外於此而得之矣。又何災變之難弭，而至治之難
translation_en:
…The yellow dragon bearing up the boat was Heaven’s means of warning Yu. In his single utterance, “I exert all my strength and toil for the people,” how complete was Yu’s reverence for Heaven! The seven-year drought was Heaven’s means of warning Tang. In those few words of self-reproach at the Mulberry Grove, how complete was Tang’s respect for Heaven! As for mediocre rulers and benighted sovereigns, they sever themselves from Heaven; Heaven, too, loathes and abandons them. Why would it still send them warnings?

I have humbly heard that whenever calamities and anomalies occur, our sage Son of Heaven trembles in apprehension and rouses himself to vigilance, allowing himself no respite from dawn to dusk. Surely this shows that he tacitly understands Heaven’s intention and preserves a heart that reveres Heaven. Yet although arrears have been remitted, measures to enrich the treasury have not been fully implemented; although fraudulent and excessive grants have been abolished, the avenues for soliciting imperial favors have not been entirely closed; although predatory strongmen have been restrained, those who pursue illicit profit still harbor hopes of undeserved gain; and although worthy men living in obscurity have been summoned to office, those who offer counsel sometimes suffer dismissal and exclusion. Might it be that reverence for Heaven is still not fully realized, and that the means of averting anomalies have likewise not been fully employed?

I humbly beseech our sage Son of Heaven to implement these policies with the firmness of metal and stone, to maintain them with the constancy of the four seasons, and to administer them equitably, with the impartiality of Heaven and Earth. Let reverence at the outset not depend upon the occurrence of calamity, nor let the absence of calamity lead to negligence in the end. Then this single resolve to revere Heaven will be the very heart with which Yu the Great exerted all his strength and toiled for the people, and with which Cheng Tang offered prayers at the Mulberry Grove. The means of moving Heaven will be found in this alone. Why, then, should calamities and anomalies be difficult to avert, and perfect government difficult to…

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
期哉然格天固在於君而輔君尤在於臣
蓋君有畏天之心而臣能將順之是引君
以道也君無慢天之心而臣先導之是逢
君之惡也引君者其心忠逢君者其罪大
此李沆災異之奏所以有聖人之稱而天
變不足畏之王安石所以得罪於萬世也
愚也負芹曝之懷久矣倘得預序事之列
請執是說以往
第五問
苗汝霖
同考試官教諭林　批〔四事中又提出兵糧爲重　語平而意深眞善於論事者非胸中素有濟世之具其〕
能爲此言乎是用録出
考試官教諭粘　批〔深達時政可以与世用矣〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔論時事有斟酌非徒作者〕
爲政之道在於行法亦在於通變法立而
不行則爲虛文雖善不足以濟事法窮而
不變則爲執一而有不可久也行法在舉
punctuated:
期哉？然格天固在於君，而輔君尤在於臣。蓋君有畏天之心，而臣能將順之，是引君以道也；君無慢天之心，而臣先導之，是逢君之惡也。引君者，其心忠；逢君者，其罪大。此李沆災異之奏所以有聖人之稱，而天變不足畏之王安石所以得罪於萬世也。愚也負芹曝之懷久矣，倘得預序事之列，請執是說以往。

第五問
苗汝霖

同考試官教諭林，批〔四事中又提出兵糧爲重，語平而意深，眞善於論事者。非胸中素有濟世之具，其〕能爲此言乎？是用録出。
考試官教諭粘，批〔深達時政，可以与世用矣。〕
考試官教諭劉，批〔論時事有斟酌，非徒作者。〕

爲政之道，在於行法，亦在於通變。法立而不行，則爲虛文，雖善不足以濟事；法窮而不變，則爲執一，而有不可久也。行法在舉
translation_en:
…to attain? Yet moving Heaven certainly rests with the ruler, while assisting the ruler rests above all with his ministers. When a ruler has a heart that fears Heaven and his ministers support and foster it, this is guiding the ruler by the Way. When a ruler has no thought of slighting Heaven but his ministers lead him toward it, this is encouraging evil in the ruler. Those who guide the ruler are loyal at heart; those who encourage his evil incur great guilt. Thus Li Hang, through his memorials on calamities and anomalies, earned the appellation of sage, whereas Wang Anshi, who held that changes in Heaven need not be feared, incurred the condemnation of all subsequent ages. I, in my ignorance, have long wished to offer my humble contribution, like one offering celery or the warmth of the sun. Should I gain a place among those entrusted with official duties, I ask to proceed according to this view.

Fifth Policy Question
Miao Rulin

Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: 〔Among the four matters, he further singles out troops and grain supplies as the most important. His language is plain but his meaning profound: he truly excels at discussing affairs. Unless he already possessed within himself the capacity to benefit the world, could he〕have spoken thus? For this reason, this answer has been selected for inclusion.
Examiner Nian, Instructor, comments: 〔He thoroughly understands current government affairs and can be of service to the world.〕
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔His discussion of current affairs shows careful judgment; he is no mere composer of essays.〕

The way to govern lies in implementing laws, and also in adapting to change. If laws are established but not implemented, they become empty words: however good they may be, they cannot help accomplish anything. If laws reach the limits of their usefulness but are not changed, this amounts to rigid adherence to a single course and cannot endure. Implementing laws lies in putting into effect…

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
其實而屬於初通變在因於時而不悖於
法其要又在於任人而已然則今之治效
之未著者其行法之未至乎亦猶有當通
變者乎
聖天子即位之初即蠲逋賦減田租以佐貧民
省浮費革冗食以足國用除債帥以恤邉
士脩馬政以給騎兵法至善也
恩至渥也而臣下之竭力從事以期效者亦逾
年矣然民貧財乏兵弱馬耗誠如執事之
===
所憂者愚生未達經國之務然以耳目之
所及則知其由矣憔悴之餘而繼以歲之
不易是以民之貧也然不可以罪歲不有
弊政之未革者乎贓吏之未黜者乎虗耗
之後而重以供億之煩是以財之匱也然
不可以咎往不有已徵而侵漁者乎當徵
而逋負者乎兵之不振以食之不足也然
撫恤不可以不至威令不可以不行馬之
不克以損失之素多也然羸瘠不可以不
punctuated:
其實而屬於初，通變在因於時而不悖於法，其要又在於任人而已。然則今之治效之未著者，其行法之未至乎？亦猶有當通變者乎？
聖天子即位之初，即蠲逋賦，減田租，以佐貧民；省浮費，革冗食，以足國用；除債帥，以恤邉士；脩馬政，以給騎兵。法至善也，恩至渥也，而臣下之竭力從事以期效者亦逾年矣。然民貧財乏，兵弱馬耗，誠如執事之所憂者。愚生未達經國之務，然以耳目之所及，則知其由矣。憔悴之餘，而繼以歲之不易，是以民之貧也。然不可以罪歲，不有弊政之未革者乎？贓吏之未黜者乎？虗耗之後，而重以供億之煩，是以財之匱也。然不可以咎往，不有已徵而侵漁者乎？當徵而逋負者乎？兵之不振，以食之不足也。然撫恤不可以不至，威令不可以不行。馬之不克，以損失之素多也。然羸瘠不可以不
translation_en:
…their practical substance, and pertains to the outset [?]. Adapting to change consists in responding to the times without contravening the laws. The essential point, moreover, lies simply in entrusting responsibilities to the right people. If so, is the present failure to achieve conspicuous results in government due to incomplete implementation of the laws? Or are there still matters requiring adaptation?
At the beginning of his reign, the sagely Son of Heaven remitted tax arrears and reduced land taxes to assist the poor; curtailed unnecessary expenditure and eliminated superfluous recipients of state support to provide adequately for state expenses; removed commanders who had incurred debts to obtain their posts, to care for frontier soldiers; and improved horse administration to supply the cavalry. These laws are supremely good, and this grace supremely generous. His officials have now spent more than a year exerting themselves to carry out these measures in the hope of achieving results. Yet the people remain poor, funds scarce, troops weak, and horses depleted—just as you, honored examiners, fear.
I, an ignorant student, have not mastered the business of governing the realm. Yet from what I have seen and heard, I know the causes. The people’s exhaustion has been followed by difficult harvest years: hence their poverty. Yet we cannot blame the harvests. Are there not harmful policies still unreformed, and corrupt officials still undismissed? Depletion of resources has been compounded by burdensome provisioning demands: hence the shortage of funds. Yet we cannot lay the blame on the past. Are there not revenues already collected that have been embezzled, and revenues due for collection that remain unpaid? The troops’ lack of vigor results from inadequate food. Yet care and relief must be thorough, and authoritative commands must be enforced. The inadequacy of the horse supply results from persistently heavy losses. Yet, with regard to lean and wasted horses, one must not fail to …

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
稽而倒損不可以不補此執事所謂弊乆
而不可卒振與奉行之未至而愚生所謂
行法者也慨自
先朝人心玩愒其至於今餘風未殄有司以
簿書爲職邊將以保守爲功澤壅而不流
威䙝而不振必率作而飭厲之凡有興革
責以實效去闒茸陟賢能然後人知警畏
而法行矣然兵糧猶爲今日之所急而復
有所當議者竊聞山西歲支之數計凡二
===
百二十六萬歲額所出僅一百九十四萬
則巳缺二十八萬之正矣昔以邊事之急
宣府借支二十七萬迄今僅反其半則又
出十餘萬矣雖有鹽利不能補其十一而
又不常是以
宗室之祿未敷軍士之糧恒缺借彼移此終
無所濟
天枝之繁衍日多稅糧之制額有限數年之
後雖盡山西之財賦不足以供此非有司
punctuated:
稽，而倒損不可以不補。此執事所謂弊乆而不可卒振與奉行之未至，而愚生所謂行法者也。慨自先朝，人心玩愒，其至於今，餘風未殄。有司以簿書爲職，邊將以保守爲功，澤壅而不流，威䙝而不振。必率作而飭厲之，凡有興革，責以實效，去闒茸，陟賢能，然後人知警畏而法行矣。
然兵糧猶爲今日之所急，而復有所當議者。竊聞山西歲支之數，計凡二百二十六萬，歲額所出僅一百九十四萬，則巳缺二十八萬之正矣。昔以邊事之急，宣府借支二十七萬，迄今僅反其半，則又出十餘萬矣。雖有鹽利，不能補其十一，而又不常。是以宗室之祿未敷，軍士之糧恒缺，借彼移此，終無所濟。天枝之繁衍日多，稅糧之制額有限，數年之後，雖盡山西之財賦，不足以供。此非有司
translation_en:
…be inspected, and losses through death must be made good. These are what you, sir, describe as longstanding abuses that cannot be remedied at once and failures to carry out commands fully; they are what I, your humble student, mean by enforcing the laws. Lamentably, since the previous reign, people have grown negligent and given to procrastination, and this lingering habit has not yet disappeared. The responsible officials regard paperwork as their duty, while frontier commanders count merely holding their positions as an achievement. Beneficence is obstructed and fails to reach the people; authority is treated with contempt and cannot assert itself. They must be led into action, admonished, and spurred on. In every undertaking to institute improvements or abolish abuses, they must be held accountable for tangible results. Dismiss the worthless and promote the worthy and capable: only then will people learn vigilance and fear, and the laws be enforced.
Yet military provisions remain an urgent concern today, and there is a further matter requiring discussion. I have heard that Shanxi’s annual expenditure totals 2,260,000, while its annual revenue quota yields only 1,940,000, thus already leaving a shortfall of 280,000 in the regular amount [?—the stated figures imply 320,000; no unit is specified]. Previously, because of urgent frontier needs, Xuanfu borrowed 270,000. To this day it has repaid only half, leaving a further outlay of over 100,000 outstanding. Although there is revenue from salt, it cannot cover even one-tenth of the shortfall, and it is moreover irregular. Consequently, stipends for the imperial clan are not fully paid, and soldiers’ grain provisions are constantly deficient. Borrowing from one allocation and transferring funds to another ultimately accomplishes nothing. The imperial lineage grows more numerous by the day, while the fixed quota of grain tax is limited. After a few years, even the whole of Shanxi’s fiscal revenue will be insufficient to meet these needs. This is not something that the responsible officials…

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
敢議
廟堂之計也至於邊鎮之兵猶有可慮自京
營之留操而志頗驕自榆臺之一敗而氣
未復以驕悍難御之心而蓄怯懦不振之
氣何以禦敵況近者甘肅之兵至戕撫臣
而不忌三邊之士恒以缺食緐興怨言漸
不可長即今秋成之初宜不拘常格多方
儲蓄使邊庾克實人心安固委重大臣經
理選擇賢將振其紀綱明其法令庶乎可
===
也況戎虜出没無常邊事甚重且急此
廟堂之慮也執事所謂缺而未舉有司之不
可專而愚生所謂通變者此矣凡事必在
於先幾計當出於早定賈誼之策至武帝
而始行唐末之弊至宋初而始革故窮則
變變則通通則久前事之得失後事之鑒
也
祖宗之法無有不善而救偏補弊之道則在因
時而不失其初
punctuated:
敢議，廟堂之計也。至於邊鎮之兵，猶有可慮。自京營之留操而志頗驕，自榆臺之一敗而氣未復。以驕悍難御之心，而蓄怯懦不振之氣，何以禦敵？況近者甘肅之兵至戕撫臣而不忌，三邊之士恒以缺食緐興怨言，漸不可長。即今秋成之初，宜不拘常格，多方儲蓄，使邊庾克實，人心安固。委重大臣經理，選擇賢將，振其紀綱，明其法令，庶乎可也。況戎虜出没無常，邊事甚重且急，此廟堂之慮也。執事所謂缺而未舉、有司之不可專，而愚生所謂通變者，此矣。

凡事必在於先幾，計當出於早定。賈誼之策至武帝而始行，唐末之弊至宋初而始革。故窮則變，變則通，通則久。前事之得失，後事之鑒也。祖宗之法無有不善，而救偏補弊之道，則在因時而不失其初。
translation_en:
… dare deliberate upon; this calls for planning by the central court. As for the troops in the frontier garrisons, there are still grounds for concern. Since being retained for drill in the capital camps, they have become quite arrogant; since the defeat at Yutai [?], their morale has yet to recover. With minds arrogant, fierce, and difficult to control, yet spirits timid and unable to rally, how can they resist the enemy? Moreover, recently the troops in Gansu went so far as to murder the grand coordinator without restraint, while soldiers in the Three Border Commands constantly raise complaints over shortages of food. This tendency must not be allowed to grow. Now, just as the autumn harvest begins, provisions should be accumulated by every means, without adhering rigidly to customary procedures, so that the frontier granaries may be filled and the people's minds made secure. Entrust their management to senior ministers of standing, select worthy generals, restore military discipline, and make the laws and orders clear: then matters might be put right. Furthermore, the hostile tribes appear and disappear unpredictably, and frontier affairs are both extremely important and urgent. These are concerns for the central court. These are precisely what you, honored examiners, call neglected measures yet to be undertaken, matters on which the responsible officials cannot act alone, and what I, your humble student, call adapting through change.

In all affairs, one must anticipate the first signs of developments, and plans should be settled early. Jia Yi's proposals were not implemented until Emperor Wu's reign; the abuses of the late Tang were not reformed until the beginning of the Song. Thus, “When circumstances reach an impasse, change follows; through change comes free passage; through free passage comes endurance.” The successes and failures of earlier affairs serve as a mirror for those that follow. None of the ancestral emperors' laws is unsound; the way to correct imbalances and remedy abuses lies in adapting to the times without losing their original intent.

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
朝廷之德意已至而承流宣化之職則在舉
行而必責其效孔子曰爲政在人孟子曰
法不能以自行是以又在於得人焉耳夫
爲治之道欲速則不達然亦有緩急期月
之間固難責以治效然久則玩玩則廢況
今天下之勢如以七年之病求三年之艾
任事之臣夙夜匪懈猶恐未稱而可以耽
歲月乎惟
朝廷之上進君子退小人振紀綱明賞罰則
===
何所不肅藩省之臣稽吏弊飭官箴察民
隱宣上德則何所不治邊疆之臣厚撫恤
明號令勤教練宣威德則何所不勝然取
人以身其本又在於
君心愚生芹曝之忠非言之可盡也執事幸恕
其不諱而進之
punctuated: 朝廷之德意已至，而承流宣化之職，則在舉行而必責其效。孔子曰：「爲政在人。」孟子曰：「法不能以自行。」是以又在於得人焉耳。夫爲治之道，欲速則不達，然亦有緩急。期月之間，固難責以治效，然久則玩，玩則廢。況今天下之勢，如以七年之病求三年之艾，任事之臣夙夜匪懈，猶恐未稱，而可以耽歲月乎？惟朝廷之上，進君子，退小人，振紀綱，明賞罰，則何所不肅？藩省之臣，稽吏弊，飭官箴，察民隱，宣上德，則何所不治？邊疆之臣，厚撫恤，明號令，勤教練，宣威德，則何所不勝？然取人以身，其本又在於君心。愚生芹曝之忠，非言之可盡也。執事幸恕其不諱而進之。
translation_en:
The court’s benevolent intentions have already reached their fullest extent; the duty of those who receive its influence and spread its transforming instruction lies in putting these intentions into practice and insisting upon results. Confucius said, “The conduct of government depends upon men.” Mencius said, “Laws cannot put themselves into effect.” Thus, this too depends upon obtaining the right men. In governing, haste prevents success, yet some matters can wait while others are urgent. Within a single year, it is admittedly difficult to demand effective government; but prolonged delay breeds negligence, and negligence leads to abandonment. Moreover, the present condition of the realm resembles seeking mugwort aged for three years to treat an illness of seven years’ standing. Even if the ministers entrusted with affairs work tirelessly day and night, they still fear falling short. How, then, can they squander months and years?

If the court promotes gentlemen and dismisses petty men, invigorates discipline and order, and makes rewards and punishments clear, what will fail to be brought into order? If provincial officials investigate abuses among clerks, enforce the precepts governing official conduct, examine the people’s hidden sufferings, and spread the sovereign’s beneficence, what will fail to be well governed? If frontier officials provide generous care and relief, make commands clear, diligently conduct military training, and manifest imperial might and virtue, where will victory be lacking? Yet selecting men depends upon the ruler’s own person, and its foundation lies, in turn, in the ruler’s heart. The loyal devotion of this humble student—like the humble offerings of celery and the sun’s warmth—cannot be fully expressed in words. May you, honored examiners, forgive his frankness and recommend him for advancement.

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
山西鄉試錄後序
嘉靖壬午山西鄉試事提調
以牧職監試以憲職考校以
郡縣文學之職内外群執事
以諸屬職之良者
制也監臨則御史沈〔俊〕自以爲
職檢防周慎遴選惟精圍棘
之地舊隘以庳葺而新之表
揭崇樹至者改觀於
===
制有光焉盖自我
祖宗開創以來
列聖相承選士非一而是歲則
皇上龍飛第一科也伏覩
臨御之初柄用元臣收召遺逸
punctuated:
山西鄉試錄後序

嘉靖壬午山西鄉試事，提調以牧職，監試以憲職，考校以郡縣文學之職，内外群執事以諸屬職之良者，制也。監臨則御史沈〔俊〕自以爲職，檢防周慎，遴選惟精。圍棘之地，舊隘以庳，葺而新之，表揭崇樹，至者改觀，於制有光焉。盖自我祖宗開創以來，列聖相承，選士非一，而是歲則皇上龍飛第一科也。伏覩臨御之初，柄用元臣，收召遺逸，
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shanxi Provincial Examination

For the Shanxi Provincial Examination in the renwu year of Jiajing [1522], local administrative officials served as Proctors, surveillance officials supervised the examination, and prefectural and county educational officials evaluated the papers. The various attendants inside and outside the examination compound were chosen from capable subordinate officials. Such was the prescribed system. Censor Shen Jun personally assumed responsibility as Supervising Official. His inspections and precautions were thorough and careful, and his selection of candidates exacting. The examination compound, enclosed by thorn fencing, had formerly been cramped and low; he repaired and renewed it. Markers and notices were prominently erected [?], giving those who arrived a transformed view and lending distinction to the established system.

Since our founding ancestors established the dynasty, successive sage sovereigns have selected scholars on many occasions. This year, however, marked the first examination since His Majesty ascended the throne. We humbly observe that, at the beginning of his reign, he entrusted authority to senior ministers and summoned worthy men who had remained outside official service…

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
如恐弗逮繼
策多士於
廷疇咨以中興之務人心已躍
焉思奮矣邇復
臨視大學禮重儒臣坐講經史
所以風示天下者益厚以周
治理之會於是一新選士之
===
典亦視昔爲盛率而行之於
御史者至矣而服勤報稱之
道非諸士子之所宜自勵耶
夫言足以發天下之理者文
也力足以任天下之重者才
也道足以輔天下之治者德
也德著而爲才才散而爲文
punctuated:
如恐弗逮，繼策多士於廷，疇咨以中興之務，人心已躍焉思奮矣。邇復臨視大學，禮重儒臣，坐講經史，所以風示天下者益厚以周，治理之會於是一新。選士之典亦視昔爲盛，率而行之，於御史者至矣，而服勤報稱之道，非諸士子之所宜自勵耶？
夫言足以發天下之理者，文也；力足以任天下之重者，才也；道足以輔天下之治者，德也。德著而爲才，才散而爲文。
translation_en:
…as though fearing he could not reach them all. He then examined the many scholars at court with policy questions, consulting them on the tasks of dynastic restoration. People’s hearts were already stirred, and they aspired to exert themselves. Recently, he also visited the Imperial University, accorded high ceremonial respect to Confucian officials, and sat to discuss the Classics and histories. The example he thereby set for all under Heaven became still more substantial and comprehensive, and the prospects for good government were thus renewed. The institution for selecting scholars likewise flourished more than in former times. The Censor has been most thorough in observing and implementing it. Is not diligent service in fitting recompense something in which all you scholars ought to spur yourselves onward?
Writing is that whose words suffice to reveal the principles of all under Heaven; ability is that whose strength suffices to bear the weighty responsibilities of all under Heaven; virtue is that whose Way suffices to support the governance of all under Heaven. Virtue manifests itself as ability, and ability finds expression as writing…

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
非二物也傳稱山西士淳儉
好學蓋有唐虞及臯陶傳說
之風敎焉茲觀三試之文淡
而雋平而婉質而理壯而肅
則信有然者是固進德之資
非但才焉而已也德以輔世
才以充之如臯陶之知人安
民以賛重華之治傳說之納
誨輔德以致允恊之休斯學
之全功也若徒詑夫文焉以
為進身之階豈所望於士也
哉抑嘗竊聞之治世之氣盛
夫北而漸夫南聖人之化由
夫近以及夫遠儒者之學勤
punctuated:
非二物也。傳稱山西士淳儉好學，蓋有唐虞及臯陶、傳說之風敎焉。茲觀三試之文，淡而雋，平而婉，質而理，壯而肅，則信有然者。是固進德之資，非但才焉而已也。德以輔世，才以充之。如臯陶之知人安民，以賛重華之治；傳說之納誨輔德，以致允恊之休，斯學之全功也。若徒詑夫文焉，以為進身之階，豈所望於士也哉？

抑嘗竊聞之：治世之氣盛夫北而漸夫南，聖人之化由夫近以及夫遠，儒者之學勤
translation_en:
…are not two separate things. Traditional accounts describe the scholars of Shanxi as honest, frugal, and devoted to learning, preserving something of the moral influence and teaching of Tang Yao and Yu Shun, Gao Yao, and Fu Yue (transcribed as 傳說). Looking now at the compositions from the three examination sessions, I find them unadorned yet rich in meaning, even in tone yet graceful, plain yet reasoned, vigorous yet dignified. These accounts are indeed borne out. Such writing is surely a foundation for advancing in virtue, rather than merely a display of talent. Virtue serves the world, and talent gives it full effect. Gao Yao understood men and brought peace to the people, thereby assisting the government of Chonghua [Shun]; Fu Yue offered instruction and fostered virtue, thereby bringing about the blessings of true harmony. These exemplify the full achievement of learning. If scholars merely boast of their writing and use it as a stepping-stone to advancement, can this be what we expect of them?

Moreover, I have heard that the vital influence of an age of good government flourishes in the north and gradually spreads southward; the transforming influence of the sage proceeds from what is near to what is distant; and the learning of Confucian scholars requires diligence…

title: 嘉靖元年山西鄉試錄
text:
於已以率於人山西直參井
之墟北邇畿甸所謂氣之淑
化之純盖全鍾而厚被者矣
會斯道之全以弼成中興之
治爲天下先是非諸士子之
責耶侈而大之將爲是邦之
科第榮則御史求賢意也嗚
===
呼念之哉
浙江杭州府仁和縣儒學教
諭粘爍謹序
punctuated:
於已以率於人。山西直參井之墟，北邇畿甸，所謂氣之淑、化之純，盖全鍾而厚被者矣。會斯道之全，以弼成中興之治，爲天下先，是非諸士子之責耶？侈而大之，將爲是邦之科第榮，則御史求賢意也。嗚呼，念之哉！
浙江杭州府仁和縣儒學教諭粘爍謹序。
translation_en:
…in oneself, so as to lead others by example. Shanxi lies beneath the celestial fields of Shen and Jing and, to the north, near the capital region. What are called the excellence of vital influences and the purity of civilizing transformation are surely concentrated here in their fullness and bestowed in abundance. To comprehend this Way in its entirety, to assist in bringing about the governance of dynastic resurgence, and to take the lead throughout the realm—is this not the responsibility of you scholars? To extend and magnify this achievement, thereby bringing honor to this province through examination success: this is the Censor’s intention in seeking worthy men. Ah, reflect upon this!
Preface respectfully composed by Nian Shuo, Instructor of the Confucian School of Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang.
